#4511. Car Body Styles and Sizes Explained, from Compact Sedans to Full-Size SUVs and Everything in Between

If you’re looking understand the difference between a coupe and a sedan, or even between a compact SUV and a mid-size SUV, let us break it down.

The term "body style" is an all-encompassing label used to describe the size, shape, and characteristics of a vehicle. For example, sedans and pickup trucks are two popular vehicle body styles in the United States. At Car and Driver, we separate vehicles into eight primary body styles, making them easier to categorize (and easier for you to shop).

Within those eight broad body styles are a host of different variations that get even more specific. Size is one of the most important distinctions. We typically categorize vehicles in the following sizes, listed in increasing order: subcompact, compact, mid-size, and full-size. There are also differences in luxury vehicles versus non-luxury vehicles, and some vehicles that defy categorization altogether. Not sure where the car you’re interested in fits? We've broken down all of the main vehicle types and their subcategories to help you understand the body style basics.

See all results for used cars for sale near ?

Sedans are what most people picture when they think of a traditional passenger car. Sedans have four doors and incorporate a three-box design (jargon for a design with a distinct hood, passenger compartment, and trunk). Sedans come in multiple types and sizes, ranging from fuel-efficient and small compact to luxurious and large full-size options.

The smallest sedans in the U.S. are subcompact in size. Among non-luxury options, there are no sedans remaining in this segment, as automakers have dropped these entry-level options. The luxury subcompact segment is more flush with options. This subset includes the Audi A3 and Mercedes CLA-class.

Compact sedans are larger than subcompacts but smaller than mid-size models. Both mainstream and luxury options abound. In either form, compacts tend to offer reasonable space for cargo and people, though taller individuals may find these models’ rear seat room a bit too confining. The Honda Civic is a benchmark of the mainstream compact segment, as it expertly blends a reasonably roomy rear seat and trunk with enjoyable driving dynamics for a reasonable price. It’s why the model’s practically a regular on our 10Best Cars.

Mid-size sedans tend to sacrifice some of the driving enjoyment of their compact kin for additional rear seat and cargo space. These machines are perfect for those who regularly carry passengers or haul various items. The best mid-size sedans afford this extra versatility with only a marginal hit to behind-the-wheel joy. This includes the 10Best-winning Honda Accord in the mainstream segment and vehicles such as the BMW 5-series in the mid-size luxury segment.

Full-size sedans these days are the flagship models in a brand’s lineup. Only luxury-badged full-size sedans remain, as previous mainstream full-size options such as the Ford Taurus were discontinued years ago. The luxurious Mercedes-Benz S-class is a prime example of the category. Such sedans tend to emphasize a comfortable ride and loads of rear seat space above all else.

See all results for used cars for sale near ?

Sports sedans come in subcompact, compact, mid-size, and full-size forms. These models tend to be high-performance variants of more run-of-the-mill models, though some may argue that a number of these “run-of-the-mill” options are sports sedans in and of themselves. For instance, the subcompact Cadillac CT4 and compact Cadillac CT5 feature engaging rear-drive dynamics that arguably make these sedans worthy of the title. However, we limit the sports sedan designation to the models' truly sporty 10Best-winning CT4-V Blackwing and CT5-V Blackwing variants.

Sport utility vehicles, better known as SUVs, are the most popular vehicle type in the United States. This is in large part due to their versatility. Most SUVs offer generous space in the cabin and cargo area. They’re also offered in a variety of forms, from wagon-like crossover SUVs to hardcore off-road ones. Some are even capable of holding their own on the track.

Subcompact SUVs are the smallest of the breed. These typically inexpensive SUVs (relatively speaking, of course) often offer middling room for rear seat passengers or cargo, but do include the higher seating position and extra ground clearance that SUVs are associated with. Like their sedan stablemates, these models are available in both mainstream and luxury guises. While some subcompact SUVs feel more like penalty boxes, others, such as the 10Best-winning Chevrolet Trax, do a great job of making these entry-level machines feel anything but.

Compact SUVs—for example, the 10Best-winning Honda CR-V,—are effectively modern-day station wagons, combining reasonable rear seat and cargo space with a manageably sized footprint. Most mainstream compact SUVs are relatively affordable, and the best examples offer a versatile interior in a reasonably fun-to-drive package. On the other end of the spectrum, the 10Best-winning Porsche Macan trades interior space and versatility for dynamics that rival those of the best sports cars. In between sit luxury compact SUVs like the Genesis GV70, which combine luxurious wares with a comfortable ride and a generally playful chassis for once the roads start to turn.

Mid-size SUVs often have more passenger and cargo space. They also tend to offer a more premium feel, though both mainstream and luxury options are available. Some mid-size models offer just two rows of seats; while these choices offer the same five-passenger seating capacity as compact SUVs in most cases they have more space behind the rear seats for cargo when compared with a compact SUV. A prime example of a two-row, mid-size SUV is the Honda Passport.

Many mid-size SUVs are available with three rows of seats, providing seating for six, seven, or eight passengers depending on the configuration. The 10Best-winning Kia Telluride exemplifies the mid-size three-row category.

Full-size SUVs take advantage of their substantial dimensions, providing generous space for passengers and their stuff, as well as formidable towing capabilities. General Motors' Chevrolet Tahoe and GMC Yukon are two notable examples.

Crossover SUVs are available in all shapes and sizes, and many of the models we’ve already discussed are categorized as crossovers. Unlike traditional SUVs, which ride on truck-like body-on-frame underpinnings, crossover SUVs including the Honda CR-V use car-like unibody construction. The result is a vehicle that looks like an SUV (and in some instances, performs as well as an SUV—such as the Jeep Grand Cherokee and Land Rover Discovery) and offers the high seating position and—typically—the ground clearance of an SUV, but combines the maneuverability and ride comfort typically associated with cars.

Unlike traditional passenger cars that have a separate trunk around back, hatchbacks combine the passenger compartment and cargo hold into one continuous area. In place of a trunk lid, hatchbacks have a flip-up tailgate, called a "hatch," that can be raised to expose a large storage compartment behind the seats. Hatchbacks typically have either two or four passenger doors plus the hatch, which automakers often classify as an additional door.

The appeal of a rear hatch is rooted in practicality, and that is exactly what traditional hatchbacks are known for. Some models, like the Honda Civic, come in both sedan and hatchback body styles, the latter affording additional cargo volume.

Hot hatchbacks inject some adrenaline into the traditional hatchback formula. Models like the Volkswagen Golf R and Honda Civic Type R are fitted with potent engines and other go-fast features while retaining a rear hatch. That combination makes them equally usable for hefty grocery store runs and weekend track days.

Like sedans, coupes feature a three-box form. Unlike sedans, which feature four doors, coupes come with just two. Coupes tend to prioritize style over practicality, with attractive sloping roofs and limited rear passenger space.

Performance coupes sacrifice nearly everything in the name of high speeds and engaging handling. Two-seat sports cars like the Chevrolet Corvette and Porsche 911 GT3 RS also fall into the performance-coupe category, with mighty engines and sleek body lines being key pillars of the segment.

Luxury coupes take the two-door body style and up the extravagance with opulent cabins and high price tags. The Bentley Continental GT is an exemplar of the luxury-coupe class with quilted leather upholstery and sleek bodywork that oozes style.

In recent years, some automakers have started calling vehicles with sloping rooflines coupes, regardless of their door count or size. The Mercedes CLA-class is an example of a model that is marketed as a four-door coupe. Even some four-door SUVs, such as the BMW iX4, are sold as coupes despite the obvious contradictions.

Convertibles, often called droptops, feature a roof that folds (or drops) away into a compartment behind the passenger compartment for an unfettered view of the sky while cruising. Most convertibles have just two doors, but four-door options do exist. Some convertibles have electrically operated tops that tuck away at the push of a button, while others require the roof to be folded away and raised manually.

Softtop convertibles lack a solid roof and feature a canvas or fabric lid instead. These convertibles tend to weigh less than their hardtop-convertible counterparts.

Instead of using a soft material for the roof, hardtop convertibles feature hard body panels for a roof, which can be folded away—typically at the push of a button, as on the Chevrolet Corvette. Such a setup affords owners the benefits of open-air driving while allowing for additional protection from the elements with the roof in place, including outside noises.

Station wagons are a dying breed. Though they wear a similar shape to many squarebacked SUVs and crossovers, these typically lower-riding machines often share styling fore of the B-pillar (or from the front door forward) with an equivalent sedan in an automaker’s lineup. With no separate trunk and little to no peak in their roofline, station wagons offer a large and versatile cargo hold for hauling items of all sizes.

Luxury station wagons combine the niceties of an automaker's equivalent sedan and pair it with a more cargo-friendly wagon form.

Crossover station wagons, for instance the Audi A6 Allroad, take the basic wagon form and add a bit of (typically pseudo) off-road kit. This normally comes courtesy of unpainted plastic fascias and fender flares, a suspension lift, and standard all-wheel drive. Though these station wagons cannot replace a proper body-on-frame SUV with four-wheel drive off-road, they are capable of handling light off-tarmac terrains.

Pickup trucks are high-riding, utility-focused vehicles that feature a front passenger compartment (known as a "cab") and an open cargo bed in the rear. Most trucks offer some form of all-wheel drive system to improve their off-road and rough-weather capabilities. Pickups range in size from the compact and economical to big and heavy-duty.

Compact pickup trucks trade expansive cargo bed space for efficiency and versatility. While models like the 10Best-winning Ford Maverick and Hyundai Santa Cruz only have enough space in the back for hauling small loads, their small form factor and efficient engines grant them easy maneuverability and relatively impressive fuel economy.

Mid-size pickup trucks strike a balance between size, price, and capability. Mid-sizers such as the Toyota Tacoma and Ford Ranger typically have smaller beds and lower towing capacities than larger full-size and heavy-duty pickups; however, they trade this loss in capability for a smaller footprint and—often—a lower starting price.

Full-size pickup trucks are large and capable trucks with big beds and impressive tow ratings. They are ideal for serious work, but many full-size pickups, including the 10Best-winning Ram 1500 and Ford F-150, are comfortable enough for use as everyday vehicles.

As their name suggests, heavy-duty pickup trucks are meant for heavy hauling. HD workhorses, such as the Ram 2500 and 3500 HD and Ford F-250 and F-350 Super Duty, are easily capable of towing five-figure loads. HD pickups are often available with high-output diesel engines and can be optioned with different cab and bed sizes to suit the needs of multiple rugged professions.

Vans and minivans are known for their spacious insides and box-like exteriors. Both vans and smaller minivans are often long and tall, leaving a cavernous area behind the front seats for either passengers or cargo. Minivans almost unanimously come with one or more sliding rear doors, while bigger vans may include sliding rear doors or a pair of barn doors.

Cargo vans are made for hauling goods. Most come with just two seats, affording plenty of room for carrying cargo aft of the driver and front passenger. In many cases, cargo vans are used as commercial vehicles.

Passenger vans typically take the cargo van template but add a handful of extra exterior windows and multiple rows of rear seats to the mix. Passenger vans often serve as commercial vehicles, though those with a penchant for carrying many passengers will find lots to like in these machines, too.

As their name implies, minivans are, well, smaller-size vans. They're still plenty roomy, though, and typically offer seating for at least seven. With designs that maximize interior space, but a footprint comparable to a three-row mid-size SUV, minivans offer car-like comfort with loads of passenger and cargo room.

#4510. Kia’s EV5 spotted with an updated design and a huge new infotainment display

Kia’s Sportage-sized electric SUV, the EV5, was spotted with a distinct new style and an overhauled interior, including a huge widescreen infotainment screen.

The EV5 is the fully electric SUV we want, but can’t have in the US. After launching it in China in 2023, Kia introduced the global version last year, which is now on sale in Europe, Canada, the UK, and other markets.

It has already been a big part of Kia’s comeback in China and is expected to become one of its best-selling EVs.

Kia appears to be preparing an updated version. A new EV5 model was recently spotted by ShortsCar in a South Korean parking garage without camouflage, and it’s expected to be the updated version.

You can see in the video that the design has changed quite a bit. Up front, the hood and headlights remain about the same, but new design elements like a black accent light are added.

It also features a unique bumper design, similar to that of the rugged EV5 WKNDR Concept Kia revealed last November at the Guangzhou Motor Show.

The biggest changes are inside, where the interior appears to be completely overhauled. Instead of the current large display screen spanning from the driver to the center, the new EV5 features a display that extends from the center to the passenger side.

There also appears to be an added slim display in front of the steering wheel. Since Hyundai has recently added a slim display to vehicles equipped with its Pleos infotainment system, the updated Kia EV5 is expected to feature the new setup.

However, this is still speculation and has not been confirmed. The center console has also changed. Instead of the physical buttons, it now has a cover, giving it a cleaner overall look.

According to a sticker on the back, the updated EV5 is set to launch in the Philippines. Given Kia initially launched the EV5 in China in 2023, it will be due for a facelift around 2027.

Kia has yet to confirm whether and when it will launch the updated EV5 in other global markets, such as Europe or Korea. It will likely arrive after the China-made version, like the current EV5. We should learn more details soon.

#4509. Tesla Is Now Powering One Of Its Biggest Charging Rivals

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Superchargers aren't just a Tesla thing anymore. Today EVgo announced that it opened its first location powered by Tesla hardware. The 12-stall charging station in Chicago kicks off an expansion that will include hundreds more Supercharger stalls nationwide, EVgo said.

With the shift to the North American Charging Standard (NACS), Tesla has shifted in some aspects toward a brand-agnostic tech provider. The NACS port was once a Tesla exclusive; now it’s the port of choice when it comes to modern EVs. Similarly, Tesla’s V4 Supercharging cabinets are available for purchase and installation by any commercial client. Tesla's V4 Supercharging cabinets are powerful, offering speeds up to 500 kW.

“Deploying our first EVgo Supercharger marks an important milestone in growing our customer base while supporting the EV industry’s transition to NACS,” said EVgo CEO Badar Khan.

The first EVgo location in Chicago has both CCS and NACS ports, thanks to the Magic Dock connector. The first batch of Tesla-powered EVgo stations will be built at grocery stores and shopping outlet centers owned by real estate company Regency Centers. This developer has had a longstanding partnership with EVgo; it already had plans to implement 400 more charging stalls. It says that Illinois is a great place to start its Supercharger push, since EV registrations have grown 60% over the past two years.

One nice bonus for Tesla drivers: EVgo’s Superchargers come up in Tesla’s in-car navigation system. As long as the “third-party charging” box is checked in the Tesla navigation app, users will be able to navigate to and charge just as easily as they would for a normal Tesla Supercharging station.

EVgo’s expansion spans more than just one developer or a handful of NACS ports. The company says it already is on track to hit 500 NACS-enabled charging stations nationwide (not counting the Supercharging network). Within the next two years, it wants all of its existing stations built after 2023 to have at least one NACS plug.

Tesla isn’t the only DC fast-charging company with hardware capable of charging natively via a NACS port. Once the NACS plug shape was officially certified by SAE, charging cabinet manufacturers quickly integrated it into their designs. However, Tesla’s Supercharging cabinets are known for their reliability. Tesla itself claims that uptime is 99%, and the network is known for being one of the best in the business.

In a recent survey of EV drivers, EVgo came in second place in terms of reliability after Tesla. Implementing more Tesla Supercharging cabinets could continue to elevate EVgo's reputation.

#4508. Ford Says Even the Fathom EV’s Fanciest Trims Will Stay Under $40K

Ford says its top-spec Fathom EV truck will still start well below the average cost of a new car.

Skeptics of the Ford Fathom EV pickup have questioned Ford’s ability to provide a sub-$30,000 truck since its introduction last year, but Andrew Frick, president of Ford’s Model e division, told the Detroit Free Press that even the top trim will remain below $40,000.

After taking a prototype Fathom for a test drive last month, Ford CEO Jim Farley was reportedly blown away by the small truck’s handling and performance, calling it a “breakthrough product.” He also said the Fathom is on track to hit the market toward the end of 2027, though the team will need to keep developing at a rapid pace to get it out on time and within budget.

See all results for new 2028 Ford Fathom for sale near 19963

Ford announced the Fathom’s starting price in August. At $29,945, the pickup truck offers an affordable way to enter the EV world, and it’s the first to ride on Ford’s Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform. The Fathom is already confirmed to be equipped with a touchscreen, built-in Apple Maps, Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, and Blue Cruise hands-free driving capabilities.

The UEV platform operates on a 400-volt electrical architecture, so charging won’t be as quick as vehicles that use an 800-volt system, but Ford says the trade-off for a lighter, more affordable vehicle is worth it. It’ll also use a 48-volt system instead of the traditional 12-volt system used in most vehicles; the higher voltage is intended to increase power and fuel efficiency. Farley revealed this week that the platform will break up the electrical components into five distinct zones to simplify production processes and reduce costs.

The Fathom’s starting price puts it on the more affordable end of the entire car market, including gas-powered and hybrid vehicles, but higher trim levels often bring a significantly higher price to a new car. Ford, however, is reportedly aiming to keep even the highest Fathom trim below $40,000. It’s unclear what will be included in the base model versus the higher specs, but top trims will likely have a longer range, among other upgrades.

The Fathom’s pre-order list is expected to open in the first quarter of 2027, and the truck is slated to go on sale in the last quarter of the year. Pricing beyond the Fathom’s entry point hasn’t yet been announced, but it seems even the highest trim will remain relatively affordable.

#4507. Ford’s electric pickup is suddenly selling like hotcakes at 50% off used

Once America’s most popular electric pickup, the Ford F-150 Lightning is finding a second life on the used market.

The F-150 Lightning is hard to pass up at 50% to 60% off sticker price, even used. With new models no longer available, Ford’s electric pickup is suddenly selling like hotcakes on the used market.

After the last model rolled off the assembly line last December, CEO Jim Farley said the decision to end production came as the “very high-end EVs, the $50K, 70K, $80,000 vehicles, they just weren’t selling.”

At 50% to 60% off, it now looks like a bargain in the used market. “When Ford was selling it brand new, the math was complicated,” Jimmy Douglas, CEO of Plug, a wholesale EV dealer, recently told Bloomberg.

On the used market, however, “the Lightning is 50% to 60% of the sticker price and that is really a sweet spot,” he added.

Used Ford F-150 Lightnings are selling in about 20 days, less than half the 44-day average for used vehicles in the US. According to Edmunds.com, prices are now up 4% to about $50,000 since the start of the year.

Douglass said that close to one-third of used models are sold by rival dealerships that would normally flip them back to Ford. However, many are opting to sell them directly because of demand.

Chase Norris from Colorado called the electric pickup a bargain. He purchased a used Lightning for around $40,000 and considers it a major upgrade from his previous gas F-150.

EV Group CEO and cofounder Alex Lawrence, which sells pre-owned electric vehicles, said he can’t get his hands on any reasonably priced used F-150 Lightnings currently.

He said many Lightning buyers use it as a second truck to save money during their weekly commute.

It looks essentially the same as the gas-powered F-150, offers instant torque, and produces zero tailpipe emissions, but the electric pickup failed to meet Ford’s expectations because of its higher price.

The base F-150 Lightning Pro debuted in 2021 with a starting MSRP of $39,974, but that was quickly raised to around $60,000 a year or so later.

According to Edmunds.com, the average transaction price for the F-150 Lightning in its first year of sales was $79,000 because Ford focused on higher-priced trims. The gas version’s ATP was about $19,000 less.

Even with the higher sticker price, Ford was losing a considerable amount on each Lightning it produced. In Q1 2024, Ford lost more than $100,000 on every EV it built.

Next year, Ford will take another crack at the electric pickup market with the Fathom, the first vehicle based on its “groundbreaking” new Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform.

Ford said the Fathom will start at $28,350 for the standard-range version. Even with the $1,595 delivery fee included, the electric pickup will start at under $30,000.

As the first vehicle built on its UEV platform, Ford promises the Fathom will be a step-change from its first-generation EVs.

According to Ford, the electric pickup will offer more interior space than a Toyota RAV4 and will be the first vehicle with Apple Maps directly integrated into the navigation system.

We also know the electric pickup will have a NACS port after a few prototypes were spotted charging at a Tesla Supercharger this summer.

Ford reportedly aims to sell around 100,000 Fathoms in its first year. CEO Jim Farley said on the company’s third-quarter earnings call last week that the launch remains on track for Q4 2027.

Farley called the Fathom a “breakthrough product” and said that the MSRP under $30,000 is perfect for today’s market.

At least some F-150 owners are already trading in for lower-priced options. A member of the Ford F-150 Lightning Owners Group, JF, said that although it was a great ride, “Carvana gave us just a little less than we paid new,” adding, “R2, here we come!”

When Torque News reached out, JF said he “really liked the Lightning,” but wanted something smaller. “With the current increase in resale value, the time to trade seemed right,” JF added.

The Rivian R2 (see our review) Performance with the Launch Package is now available to order starting at $57,990 with an EPA-estimated range of up to 330 miles and 656 hp. The R2 Premium will go on sale later this year, starting at $53,990

In Spring 2027, Rivian will launch the R2 Standard, starting at $44,990 with an estimated range of up to 275 miles and 350 hp.

So were they losing $100k / truck, or the average loss when all development was included ended up being $100k? Big difference. I don't believe the cost to build each one was $170k+. That makes no sense. They just priced them too high to amortize the development costs over enough vehicles to make them profitable. Every vehicle has to sell a minimum # before they start to make a profit.

Surging F-150 Lightning sales on the used market show buyers want electric pickups. But at the right price.

At $60,000 to $70,000, the Lightning wasn’t so attractive, but at $40,000 used, it suddenly is. Perhaps Ford is on to something with its next-gen EV pickup, the Fathom, set to go on sale starting at under $30,000.

Will it deliver on its promise? Ford has yet to reveal battery specs, towing capacity, range, or any other specs. We should learn more soon.

#4506. BMW Is Giving New EV Buyers $500 In Free Charging

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

BMW's latest Neue Klasse EVs push the boundaries of range and charging speed. In short, they're some damn good electric cars. Now there's another reason to buy one: free charging.

BMW on Thursday said it's offering $500 in public charging credits for 2027 electric models. It applies to the i5, i7, and iX3, and is open to drivers who buy or lease. The benefits last for one year from the car's purchase date.

Here's how the $500 breaks down. BMW says $300 of it can be redeemed at more than 15 charging networks, including Ionna, Shell Recharge, ChargePoint, and EVgo. The other $200 only applies to Ionna locations. (BMW is one of the automakers backing Ionna.)

To access the funds, drivers need to set up an account through the BMW app. Once they do that and handle payment through BMW ChargingNetwork, credits are automatically applied to eligible charging purchases.

BMW is also offering buyers of 2027 EVs one free year of Ionna membership, which gets drivers 25% discounts on sessions at the fast-growing charging player.

If $500 in free charging sounds nice and you're considering these vehicles, I have one note of caution after getting behind the wheel of all three.

The i5 is a solid all-around EV. It drives well, looks familiar, and offers over 300 miles of range in some trims. But the i7 and iX3 are miles ahead in terms of onboard technology and specs. The latter models use BMW's Neue Klasse architecture and feature an overhauled digital interface with a wonderful "Panoramic Vision" display below the windshield. The iX3 offers over 400 miles of range and 400 kilowatt charging. Expect similar capabilities to trickle throughout BMW's lineup and into the next iteration of the i5 too.

#4504. 10 Pokémon That Are the Biggest Green Flags

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

There have been many Pokémon over the years. When you combine all the generations, there are over 1,000 different Pokémon, and each one is bound to be somebody’s favorite.

Of course, not every Pokémon conveys a positive message. There are some Pokémon, who, when mentioned as someone’s favorite, give off some major red flags.

On the other hand, there are Pokémon that also give off some major green flags. These are Pokémon that show you can trust a person. Maybe they are motherly, maybe they are a great friend, or maybe they are as innocent as can be. Either way, they are great to have around.

Mew is a classic Pokémon that is usually loved by everyone in the fan base, with few people considering it a negative sign. The reason for this is that Mew is just a little guy who is generally sweet towards others.

If you take one look at Mew, you can easily tell that it is a green flag. It looks absolutely harmless, and wouldn’t hurt a fly unless it was specifically required to do so.

With Mew being so harmless, anyone who chooses this Pokémon as their favorite is considered to be a sweet and empathetic individual who just wants to be around others because it makes them happy.

Mimikyu somewhat tows the line between a red flag and a green flag, but I am here to tell you that this Pokémon is for sure a green flag. The argument about it being a red flag is mostly because it is trying too hard to be Pikachu.

However, if you choose Mimikyu as your favorite Pokémon, it is probably because you have the emotional intelligence to identify with Mimikyu and recognize that it just wants to be loved.

It is a misunderstood creature who dresses up as Pikachu to hopefully one day get the love it rightfully deserves, which makes those who love this Pokémon people who recognize it for what it is, and realize that it is a lonesome creature who just wants to be seen.

Some Pokedex entries in the Pokemon series are pretty brutal, and these are the saddest.

The legendary beast trio from generation two are some of the most recognizable legendary Pokémon from the franchise. While each of these Pokémon are a green flag, I chose Entei to represent them because I feel like it is the most well-liked.

The legendary beasts are a great pull from the second generation of Pokémon that are well-known enough that it isn’t weird, and they aren’t obscure enough that it feels like you are trying too hard.

Each of the legendary beasts are known for being protectors, but Entei has the greatest appearance of them, coming off as more of a large fluffy lion, giving it more of the guardian vibes that people who love this Pokémon may themselves embody.

Wooloo is a more recent pull from generation eight, as the Pokémon made its first appearance in Pokémon Sword and Shield. Those who have played these games know that Wooloo are found in plenty of places early in the game, with its white wool covering the fields of Paldea.

Wooloo is an innocent little buddy who is calm, doesn’t want to go into a fight, and would rather just chill. Its little pigtails that hang along the sides of its face make it even more approachable.

Those who love this Pokémon are perceived as loving, calm, and big softies who wouldn’t want to fight unless it's absolutely necessary. The only one that is a red flag is Hop’s Wooloo, and that’s only because it beat me in the game that one time.

Every pocket monster in Pokopia is beautiful in its own way, but some are cuter than others.

Teddiursa has been around for a long time. In fact, it has been in the games since generation two, meaning fans have had a long time with this Pokémon, and there are some who consider it their favorite.

You’ll notice that many of the Pokémon on this list match the theme of “little guys,” and that is because they are so sweet and innocent that you don’t need to worry about them. Teddiursa is one of them, where it just wants to play around and eat some honey.

Those who love Teddiursa have a cute and playful side. They are also generally viewed as non-toxic because they would rather just have fun and cozy up by the fire with a good book.

There is a theme of Pokémon who are considered the “derpy” ones, and Fuecoco falls very specifically into that category. It has a face that screams, “I just want to sit around and snack all day without worrying about stressful things.”

Fuecoco is the definition of someone who is ignorant to the world around them and is blissfully going about life at their own pace. They have little care in the world and that is perfectly fine because it makes them happy.

There’s little that could be considered wrong with someone who likes Fuecoco. Maybe they are a bit too childish at times, but they are overall just a good person who lives the way they want.

Lapras is one of Ash’s Pokémon from the anime, and a Pokémon that stands out from the first generation. It is cute, calm, and collected, meaning it is definitely a green flag Pokémon.

If you judge the Pokémon from its Pokédex entry, you will find that it has a gentle heart, which led to many of them being caught because they rarely fight. Plus, it loves to ferry people around on its back, showing that you pride yourself on being there for others.

Additionally, Lapras is an overall intelligent Pokémon that is capable of understanding human speech, and those who choose it as their favorite Pokémon are often showing that they are caring, intelligent, and emotionally available friends who just want to be there for their pals.

There are some Pokémon where it feels like you chose it to be cool or to follow a trend. Cough. Charizard. Cough. Then there are some Pokémon where you love them despite the popularity, accepting the fact that they aren’t the best in terms of stats, but rather, they are just cute.

Eevee is one of those cute Pokémon that is beloved by everyone, and some choose Eevee as their favorite because of how adorable it is. Also, an argument can be made about its potential, with those who love this Pokémon showing that they believe they have great potential in life in the same way Eevee does through its evolutions.

This is a safe, friendly, and easy pick for many. It may be a bit too basic for some, but the cute factor solidifies it as a top-tier green flag.

Psyduck is a great choice for a favorite Pokémon, and is a major green flag. I am totally not saying that because it is one of my favorites, but rather because it is relatable.

This Pokémon suffers from constant headaches, which many can relate to because of the stresses of life constantly feeling like they're weighing them down. Psyduck feels like the embodiment of what is in people’s minds when dealing with stress, and it feels like an outlet in a sense.

Plus, Psyduck has some of the cutest expressions, with it often conveying confusions, annoyance, and more. If you love Psyduck, you probably aren’t toxic, have a decent sense of humor, and can be a bit childish. Now, I will pat myself on the back.

The biggest green flag of the entire Pokédex belongs to two Pokémon, and they are Wooper and Quagsire. Since I can only choose one, I went with Quagsire. After all, it is just a bigger version of Wooper.

We need to give those who love Quagsire a big hug and thank them for being some of the most chill and down to Earth people out there, as this choice of favorite is one that shows that they have the ability to just go with the flow, accepting life as it is.

Quagsire is the definition of a Pokémon that just doesn’t care about the stresses of life and lets them slide off its body and into the water it floats around in. Thanks for being such a special soul Quagsire, and keep up that chill lifestyle.

From the Eevee evolutions to Magikarp becoming something useful, here are the Pokémon in FireRed and LeafGreen that feel different after evolving.

#4503. E-quipment highlight: Jungheinrich launches new forklift for Asian markets

Like many equipment brands, German forklift maker Jungheinrich has been struggling to crack the Asian industrial markets – but the company is set to change all that with the launch of a new line of 1.6- to 3-ton class electric forklifts designed specifically to navigate the region’s tight warehouses and factories.

Jungheinrich launched the next generation of its EFG MB and MC electric counterbalance forklifts, giving businesses more flexibility to match truck performance with the battery options, charging systems, and operator features that meet their specific needs.

“Different operations have different requirements,” said Lisa Jing Xue, Managing Director at Jungheinrich’s Qingpu Plant, China. “With the EFG M series, customers can configure the (forklift) truck around their application, workload and operators – whether they need greater maneuverability for confined warehouse spaces, or a stable, powerful truck for demanding transport and stacking work.”

Forklift buyers can choose between two performance packages, prioritizing energy efficiency for everyday material handling or more driving and lifting muscle for more demanding, high-throughput operations. The higher-performance package comes standard on models rated for 2.5-3.0 tons, with a choice of either lead-acid or lithium-ion batteries with 346 or 690 Ah of capacity available to suit different workloads and shift patterns. Both ship with regenerative braking tech that can recover up to 30% of the energy used in stopping and lowering loads, too, helping to keep these machines running longer between charging sessions.

“We carried out extensive customer research to understand what the market needs,” added Jing Xue. “Customers can invest in the performance required today and add further capabilities as their application demands.”

Optional features include fingertip controls, a larger 4″ digital display, upgraded LED lighting, and operator-assistance (ADAS) systems, while flexible seating and cabin configurations are designed to keep drivers comfortable through long shifts. A slim B-pillar and glass roof help visibility in busy warehouses, while the four-wheel EFG MC gets automatic cornering speed reduction as standard. Integrated telematics are also standard, giving fleet managers access to utilization data, maintenance planning and pre-operational checks from day one.

Jungheinrich says the order books for both the three- and four-wheel electric forklifts are open now, ready to be supported by the company’s 6,000+ person strong service network across the Asia-Pacific region.

#4502. 2027 Lamborghini Temerario

See all results for new 2027 Lamborghini Temerario for sale near 29405

The Temerario might be the runt of the Lamborghini supercar litter, but it's still one raging bull. Taking the reins from its widely lauded Huracan predecessor, the Temerario is the least expensive way into Lambo's supercar lineup, but it doesn’t sacrifice much performance compared to the company's Revuelto flagship—in fact, it beats its brawnier older brother to 60 mph by a tenth of a second.

Under the Temerario's origami-folded sheetmetal lies a newly developed 4.0-liter twin-turbo V-8 nestled into the car's aluminum spaceframe just ahead of the rear axle. As if 789 horsepower from the engine alone wasn’t enough, a trio of electric motors—one mounted between the engine and transmission and one at each front wheel—ups its total output to 907 Italian stallions. If you somehow tire of the sound of the flat-plane-crank V-8's goosebump-raising 10,000-rpm wail, the electric motors also allow for short periods of silent, all-electric driving. With its mighty hybrid-assisted thrust, poster-worthy looks, and agile moves, the Temerario is every inch a purebred Lambo and well worthy of supercar status.

Expert Tip: If you'd rather have a horse instead of a bull in your garage, the Ferrari 296GTB is a steed with the need for speed, and moves to match the Lambo for a similar price.

Compare the 2027 Lamborghini Temerario with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.

Lamborghini's newest bull debuted in 2026 and charges into 2027 without any notable changes.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

The Temerario's powertrain consists of a twin-turbo 4.0-liter V-8 with a flat-plane crankshaft, a trio of axial-flux electric motors, and an eight-speed dual-clutch transmission. The Temerario's V-8 alone is good for 789 horsepower; adding the output of the three electric motors brings the total combined output to 907 horsepower. That's just 94 ponies shy of the Lamborghini Revuelto, the brand's V-12 halo car. On the Temerario, one electric motor mounts to the V-8 in front of the transmission, while the remaining two live up front, one at each wheel. The Temerario's V-8 redlines at 10,000 rpm, and the engine's peak torque of 538 pound-feet is available from 4000 to 7000 rpm. While the flat-plane-crank V-8 sounds glorious when pushed to its limit, we wish that its exhaust packed a bit more fury earlier in the rev range.

With the electric motors in play, maximum torque output rises to 590 pound-feet. In addition to supplying enormous power, the hybrid configuration helps provide instantaneous torque and linear power delivery over a broad range of speeds and driving situations. Thirteen drive programs are available via a rotary button on the steering wheel, including launch and drift modes, the latter offering three levels of tail-out leeway. We drove the Temerario at the track and on the street and were enthralled with its lively powertrain and playful demeanor.

Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.

In Comparison: In our testing, the Temerario got to 60 mph in a ridiculously quick 2.1 seconds. It also ripped through the quarter-mile in 9.4 seconds at 150 miles per hour. Both figures beat its big sibling, the Revuelto, by 0.3 seconds and 2 mph, respectively.

Juice is stored in a 3.8-kWh lithium-ion battery pack. The battery resides in the center tunnel along with the transmission—the location is said to help optimize weight distribution and is protected from underneath by structural elements. Regenerative braking and power from the internal-combustion engine both replenish the battery's state of charge. Plug-in charging is also possible via a standard 7-kW onboard charger; with typical household current, it can recharge an empty battery to full capacity in a claimed 30 minutes. An EV-only mode provides around 4 miles of range.

The EPA estimates that the Temerario will deliver 14 mpg city, 19 mpg highway, and 16 mpg combined. When we get a chance to test the Temerario, we'll update this story with results from our 75-mph highway fuel economy test. For more information about the Temerario's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

First Row: Thanks to its all-aluminum chassis, the Temerario's interior offers more space than the Huracán it replaced. Headroom increased by 1.3 inches, legroom by 1.8 inches, and Lamborghini claims the interior is large enough to accommodate drivers up to six feet five wearing a helmet. The interior shares some styling cues from the Revuelto; four stitching patterns are available, and the 18-way adjustable driver's seat is heated and ventilated. The Temerario also borrows the Revuelto's steering wheel, which is too busy with controls for our liking.

Cargo Capacity: If you're planning on taking the Temerario on a weekend getaway, you'd better pack light; the front trunk only has a four-cubic-foot capacity.

Lamborghini says the Temerario offers the most advanced suite of infotainment and connectivity features of any model in its lineup. Three displays—a 12.3-inch instrument panel with three user-selectable views, an 8.4-inch infotainment screen, and a 9.1-inch passenger screen—occupy prime dashboard real estate. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, as is a Sonus Faber audio system.

The most notable feature, though, is the optional Lamborghini Vision Unit (LAVU) system. Essentially an on-board data acquisition system, the setup utilizes three cameras: one viewing the road, one focused on the passengers, and one looking forward over the driver's shoulder. Preloaded with data for 150 different racing circuits, the system can be used to evaluate and improve driver performance. It also enables a "memories recorder" function that allows for up to two minutes of off-track recording, and works as a dashcam that can capture one minute of incident history.

Compared to most other cars, the Temerario doesn't offer many driver-assistance features.

For information about the Temerario's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

Compared with most mainstream automakers, Lamborghini doesn't provide stellar warranty coverage. But its protection plans are competitive with those of high-end rivals such as Ferrari and can be enhanced by optional extended coverage. A five-year complimentary scheduled maintenance plan is now standard.

#4501. Gas Prices Got You Down? This 261-MPG Volkswagen Solves That—For $140,000

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

In 2013, VW launched one of the most fascinating experiments in fuel efficiency ever made. The Volkswagen XL1 took 12 years to develop and ended up costing a whopping $150,000 at the time. However, as an engineering exercise, it was brilliant. And since VW only made 250, it's even rarer than a Bugatti Veyron from the same era.

If you're looking for an extreme answer to high gas prices, today's your lucky day. There's currently an XL1 in the Netherlands up for auction on Catawiki. The 2016 model up for grabs has just over 1,000 miles on the odometer and is apparently in excellent condition inside and out.

The XL1 project was spearheaded by Ferdinand Piech, VW's top boss at the time. Not known to ever give up on his lofty, ambitious goals, Piech fought for 12 years, and through several iterations, to finally achieve his "one liter" car, something that could burn just one liter of fuel per every 100 km. VW pulled out all the stops to make it extraordinarily efficient; the result was something closer to a supercar than a Toyota Prius.

That teardrop-shaped body is made from carbon fiber, as is its chassis, saving weight. It debuted a full year before BMW's i3, an EV/PHEV which only had a carbon chassis but a plastic body. The car has butterfly doors and two seats that are offset to optimize the car's aerodynamic shape.

Power comes from an 800cc, two-cylinder, turbo-diesel engine behind the driver—this makes it mid-engine, like a supercar—plus a plug-in hybrid system centered around a 5.5 kilowatt-hour battery. The plug-in hybrid powertrain wasn't originally planned, and didn't come about until near the end of its development, so it needed a massive 50-pound removable charging box in the trunk so you could plug it in.

With a funky hybrid powertrain, a curb weight of just 1,852 pounds, and a drag coefficient of just 0.189, the XL1 was capable of an EU-tested 0.9 liters per 100 km, which equates to 261 mpg. It can also travel 31 miles on battery power alone, registering an insane efficiency of 6.2 miles per kWh, about double today's more conventional EVs. VW said at the time of the XL1's launch that it only needed about 8 horsepower to sustain a steady 62 mph.

The main downside is performance: It only makes 68 horsepower, so it takes almost 13 seconds to get to 60 mph.

This specific car up for auction is expected to fetch around $140,000, according to the auction house. So even with its incredible fuel economy and currently outrageous fuel prices, the XL1's financial breakeven point is still a long ways away. Plus, it runs on diesel, which has seen even steeper price spikes than regular gas. A used EV cuts you off from the gas station entirely, and is a better all-around choice of course.

But for someone who wants an amazing piece of automotive history, the XL1 could be worth the price. Plus, it'll sip on fuel like no other for many of your daily errands—and look cool doing it.

#4500. Janus Electric secures battery supply deal for its battery-swap semi truck

Australian conversion specialists Janus Electric have been celebrating a growing slate of orders for their Class 8 electric truck conversions, which ditch diesel in favor of advanced battery-swap electric power – but exactly how they’d deliver all those trucks was still a question. Now, we have an answer: Electrovaya will supply the batteries.

The concept of dropping an electric power unit into a Class 8 semi makes perfect sense, as most of these trucks are built as gliders. That is, rolling body and chassis without an engine and transmission that’s ready to receive power from Cummins, Detroit, International, or Volvo Penta. That’s the role that Janus Electric sees itself occupying, and it seems to be working.

Janus’ reservation book crept past 70 units this past summer, helped along in part by California’s HVIP Program and the US EPA’s Diesel Emission Reduction Act (DERA) Grants. When the HVIP voucher is combined with the Port of Los Angeles’ “Plus” support, customers can received up to $166,000 per truck conversion. Factor in the massive fuel savings of electric and the classic good looks of square-nose Western Star truck body, and it’s easy to see why they’d be a popular choice.

As Jerry Seinfeld taught us however, it’s one thing to take a reservation – it’s another thing to deliver. To help make it happen, Janus has inked a battery supply deal with Electrovaya that will see a $26 million initial purchase orders for Electrovaya battery packs to demand for Janus’ products in the US and Canada, along with the battery company purchasing approximately $1.4 million in Janus stock with (what seems to be) actual money.

“Electrovaya is an important partner to Janus Electric, and we’re particularly pleased it has decided to invest directly in our business,” explains Ben Hutt, Managing Director and CEO of Janus Electric. “The investment is a strong vote of confidence in our technology and approach to electrifying heavy transport.”

The Janus Electric-repowered trucks carry a stout, 480 hp electric motor drawing power from a standard 310 kWh battery pack, with up to two battery packs (one on each side) of the truck. In practice, that gives the Janus trucks up to 370 miles of loaded range. After that, the batteries can be DC fast charged in under 90 minutes, or swapped for fresh ones in about four minutes without too much in the way of specialized equipment. That’s not just Janus’ killer app, it means that a battery supply deal like this one with a strategic partner who’s invested in the fledgling company’s success is such a huge deal.

“Reliable battery supply is critical to our growth,” adds Hutt, “and Electrovaya’s expanding North American manufacturing capabilities will be important as we scale. Both companies see considerable opportunity in this market, and we look forward to building on our partnership.”

For their part, Electrovoya executives seem to know their role here, and seem excited to be a part of what Janus is doing. “Class 8 trucking is one of the most exciting and demanding frontiers in electrification, and Janus has demonstrated real commercial traction with fleets in the US, Canada and Australia,” said Dr. Raj Das Gupta, CEO of Electrovaya. “Janus has developed a practical solution to one of the major challenges facing heavy transport, enabling diesel-powered trucks to be converted to electric without compromising their commercial operations.”

Electrovaya will be expanding its American manufacturing capacity with lithium-ion cell, module, and battery pack production at its new, potentially BABA-compliant facility in Jamestown, New York, which is expected to come online in 2027.

#4499. Mercedes Delays U.S. GLC Production, Leaving the Model Vulnerable to Tariffs

The brand’s bread-and-butter crossover won’t be made in the United States until the next generation launches.

Mercedes-Benz is delaying the start of its U.S. production of the GLC-class crossover, according to Automotive News. The automaker had originally planned for production of the GLC to begin in late 2027, but the paper reports that it has now been delayed to 2030. When the U.S. production does begin, it will take place at the automaker’s Vance, Alabama, plant.

According to the AN report, Mercedes is delaying the move in production to wait for the arrival of the next-generation GLC-class. “Investing in the plant for about half a life cycle and then having to retool for the next-generation GLC doesn’t make a lot of sense financially,” Sam Fiorani, the vice president of AutoForecast, told the outlet. The Alabama plant, in its current configuration, is home to the GLS-class and GLE-class SUVs, along with their electric counterparts.

See all results for new 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class for sale near 94043

The updated timeline lines up with the expected arrival of the next-generation GLC-class; the current model received its most recent refresh in 2023. Unfortunately, the delay leaves the GLC-class, which is one of the most important models for the brand in the United States, exposed to increased costs related to import tariffs. Mercedes has previously committed to spending some $4 billion at its Alabama plant to localize the production of its high-volume vehicles, which are currently subject to 15 percent import tariffs.

On the flip side, some reports suggest that the Trump administration is considering lowering its tariff on European cars to 10 percent in an attempt to sway Audi into building a planned $4 billion Georgia plant. Car and Driver reached out to Mercedes-Benz for confirmation of the AN report but has not heard back at the time of this article’s publication. We will update this story when we learn more.

#4498. Tesla Is Killing The Cybertruck To Make Room For More Robotaxis

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The controversial Tesla Cybertruck electric pickup will be retired next year, CEO Elon Musk confirmed on X. The angular truck went on sale at the end of 2023 and instantly became a social statement—for better or worse.

Production of the Cybertruck will start winding down next summer at the company’s Texas Gigafactory, and the extra floor space will be used to build more Cybercabs.

The unpainted truck had a short burst in popularity at the beginning of its production run, but interest fizzled, and sales never reached the potential that Musk and Tesla had envisioned back in 2019, when the vehicle was first presented as a concept.

In this year’s third quarter, the Cybertruck amassed 4,323 sales, according to data from Cox Automotive. From January through September, sales totaled 11,586 units. Tesla doesn’t break out individual sales figures for the Cybertruck, but industry estimates put the vehicle’s overall deliveries at roughly 70,000.

That’s a far cry from the hundreds of thousands of sales recorded every quarter by the Model 3 and Model Y. It’s also another reminder that electric pickups haven’t quite taken off as their manufacturers had hoped, and Tesla is now taking the fall, just like Ford did with the F-150 Lightning, which went the way of the dodo last year after lackluster sales and ballooning costs.

There’s no denying that you either love or hate the Cybertruck, just like there’s no denying that Tesla dared to do things like no other car manufacturer before it. Sure, some might argue that the angular EV looks like an unpolished fridge, but it brought steer-by-wire and a 48-volt low-voltage architecture to the masses. Whether or not they’ll be adopted by other companies is another story, though.

At roughly the same time as Elon Musk’s announcement that Cybertruck production would wind down in the middle of 2027, Tesla stopped taking orders for the entry-level Dual-Motor All-Wheel Drive version of the model, leaving just the Premium and Cyberbeast trims available to order on the automaker’s website.

Additionally, the price of the remaining models has been increased. The Premium AWD model now starts at $92,490, up from $89,990, while the top Cyberbeast now costs $102,490, up from $99,990. The most recent price bumps come after a similar move in August.

#4497. Energica rises from the ashes with plans for cheaper electric motorcycles

The Italian electric motorcycle maker, which ceased operations in 2024 after entering judicial liquidation, has announced a major revival under new international ownership. And while the Energica name is returning, the company behind it is going to look quite different this time around.

Perhaps the biggest change is where the motorcycles will actually be built.

Energica says motorcycle production is moving to Asia, while design, engineering, research and development, as well as responsibility for technical and quality standards, will remain in Italy. The new manufacturing setup is expected to significantly reduce production costs, allowing Energica to cut motorcycle prices by around 20% compared to its previous models.

That could be a big deal for a company whose motorcycles were widely praised for their performance and technology, but were also firmly positioned at the premium end of the market.

The revival comes after Energica was acquired by Energica Pte. Ltd., a Singapore-based company backed by international private investors. Importantly, much of the technological know-how isn’t disappearing overseas with the manufacturing. Energica says its core engineering and design leadership remains in Italy, including longtime CTO Giampiero Testoni and designer Paolo Imeni.

The first motorcycle to make its comeback will be the Energica Experia, the company’s adventure-oriented electric sport-tourer. After that, Energica plans to progressively restart production of the Ego, Eva Ribelle, and EsseEsse9, eventually bringing its entire previous lineup back to market.

At least initially, those motorcycles will use their existing platforms, which should help Energica get bikes rolling off the production line faster without having to develop and homologate entirely new machines. But upgrades are already planned, including a new battery and improvements to range, efficiency, performance, and reliability.

Energica is also specifically targeting Europe, the United States, and Australia as it rebuilds its dealer and service networks. Existing owners haven’t been forgotten either. The company says service has already resumed and spare-parts shipments have restarted to dealers in several countries.

For anyone who followed the electric motorcycle industry over the last decade, Energica’s disappearance was a particularly painful one. This wasn’t some startup with a couple of renderings and a dream. Energica built some of the highest-performance electric motorcycles on the road and spent four seasons supplying the motorcycles for the FIM MotoE World Cup, experience that helped develop its high-voltage and DC fast-charging technology.

Now the company gets something relatively rare in the motorcycle industry: a second chance.

And if moving production to Asia really can knock around 20% off Energica’s prices while retaining the Italian engineering that made the bikes special in the first place, Energica 2.0 might have a considerably better shot at turning great electric motorcycles into a sustainable business.

It seems like moving toward Asian manufacturing is all but inevitable here. It was the expensive European manufacturing of low-volume motorcycles that weighed so heavily on Energica’s balance sheets in the years up to their financial troubles, and so shifting production to countries with both the expertise and the cost benefits for motorcycle manufacturing simply makes sense.

Energica isn’t alone in discovering the economics of moving electric motorcycle production to Asia. Zero Motorcycles spent years manufacturing its bikes in California before beginning a major shift toward production in the Philippines in 2023, including both complete motorcycles and major subassemblies. Now the company works with multiple factories, including major manufacturers like Zongshen in China, to reduce production costs for its electric motorcycles while still maintaining the ‘designed in California’ marketing angle.

It’s too early to tell how the new strategy will play out for Energica, but the fact that the company is now following a more well-worn trail is a positive sign for those who have spent the last two years hoping for a revival.

#4495. Tesla to end Cybertruck production as sales stall at ~10% of plan

Tesla is ending Cybertruck production. CEO Elon Musk announced early Friday that the automaker will “wind down” the electric pickup at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of 2027, about three and a half years after the first deliveries.

Musk says it’s to make room for more Cybercab production. But Giga Texas isn’t short on space. The Cybertruck is short on buyers, and it sells at roughly a tenth of the 250,000 units a year Tesla built its line for.

Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production

That’s all he said. Nothing yet on how long Tesla will keep selling inventory or what happens to parts and service for existing owners.

Tesla doesn’t break out Cybertruck deliveries. It lumps them into “Other Models,” along with the Model S, Model X, and now the Semi.

That bucket tells the story anyway. Tesla delivered 8,295 “Other Models” in Q3 2026, down 48% year-over-year and the lowest since Q2 2021. With Model S and Model X production over since April, we estimated that 7,000 to 8,000 of those were Cybertrucks.

That’s a pace of about 30,000 trucks a year. Tesla planned the Cybertruck line for 250,000 units annually, and its latest shareholder letter still lists more than 125,000 units of installed capacity. So the truck is selling at about 12% of plan, and roughly a quarter of what’s actually installed.

The US numbers from Cox Automotive are worse. Cox estimates 3,519 Cybertruck sales in Q1 2026 and 3,744 in Q2, down from 14,416 in Q3 2024.

And not all of those were real customers. S&P Global Mobility data showed SpaceX bought 1,279 Cybertrucks in Q4 2025, and Musk’s companies took 1,339 in total, about 19% of US registrations that quarter. If it wasn’t for Musk’s self-dealing, the Cybertruck would probably be dead already.

Tesla tried to fix demand. It launched a cheaper rear-wheel-drive version in 2025 and pulled it months later, then brought a cheaper dual-motor trim to customers this summer. And then it raised prices by $5,000 in August. The dual-motor now starts at $74,990.

The “make room” explanation doesn’t hold up. Giga Texas has more than 10 million square feet of factory floor, by Tesla’s own count, and the Cybertruck line is already running at about a quarter of its installed capacity. Most of it is sitting idle.

The Cybercab also isn’t at a volume where it’s fighting anyone for floor space. Texas had 463 Cybercabs registered as of late October, and Tesla built a separate line for its “unboxed” manufacturing process.

If Tesla needs more Cybercab capacity down the road, it has the space. What it doesn’t want is to keep paying for a truck with its own stainless steel body, its own castings, and its own supply chain at 30,000 units a year.

Let’s call this what it is. Tesla isn’t ending the Cybertruck because the Cybercab needs room. It’s ending it because nobody’s buying it at anything close to the volume Tesla planned, and supporting a low-volume vehicle this unique is expensive.

I wouldn’t be surprised if Tesla lost a couple of billions on the Cybertruck experiment. Between R&D, pushing suppliers to produce 250,000 trucks per year, and deploying its own production line capable of 125,000 trucks per year, Tesla has invested billions. And with only ~70,000 trucks delivered in roughly 3 years, it probably never made any positive cash flow from the program.

In addition to the billions wasted on tooling, let's not forget the $50 that went into designing this thing.

The Cybercab line gives Musk a forward-looking reason to wrap a product failure in. Tesla did the same thing when it ended Model S and Model X production this year to free up Fremont for Optimus. It’s a lot easier to say “we need room for the future” than “this didn’t sell.”

We’ve said it many times: the Cybertruck is genuinely impressive to drive. Steer-by-wire and rear-wheel steering are real engineering, and nobody else has put them in a production pickup. But Tesla built a 250,000-unit factory for a polarizing $75,000+ truck that can’t be sold in Europe or most right-hand-drive markets. It just cancelled it for Australia and New Zealand two weeks ago. The math was never going to work.

It’s truly a sign of Tesla today. Musk used to talk about having a more traditional electric truck design if Cybertruck fails, but I doubt we will see that. Again, Elon is betting the house on autonomy.

#4494. Over A Quarter Of BMW, Mini, And Rolls-Royce Models Sold In Q3 Had A Plug

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The BMW Group, which operates the BMW, Mini, and Rolls-Royce car brands, saw 20% of its global vehicle sales in the third quarter represented by all-electric models. Adding plug-in hybrids increases the electrified models’ share to 27.4%, the company said in its latest earnings report.

From the beginning of the year through September, EVs have accounted for 18.4% of the three automakers’ total sales worldwide, with PHEVs raising the figure to 26.1%.

Despite the promising numbers, the automotive group clearly has a regionalization problem on its hands. Europe is leading the way by a wide margin, with 34.7% of sales represented by EVs and 46.9% by all electrified models.

Meanwhile, over in the United States, just 4.7% of BMW, Mini, and Rolls-Royce models sold were EVs. That’s a huge difference, and it puts the U.S. at the bottom of the BMW Group’s list for electrification. By comparison, Chinese EV sales amounted to 6.5%, while the Asia-Pacific, Eastern Europe, Middle East, and Africa regions totaled 18% EV sales.

The only thing that saves the day for the company’s electrified lineup in the U.S. is plug-in hybrids, which, together with EVs, had an 11.4% share in the third quarter. It’s also worth noting that the new iX3 and i3 models are just starting to trickle down to American dealers, and the U.S. also doesn’t get the electric iX2 and iX2 that Europeans have access to. The updated i7 is also on its way, but that has always been a low-volume car that never made a meaningful impact on the company’s sales reports.

What’s more, even though one in every five BMW Group models was all-electric in Q3, the company’s year-to-date numbers aren’t so promising. Globally, the group sold 314,552 EVs and 131,653 PHEVs from January through September, a 5.1% decrease compared to the same period last year. EVs saw a 2.7% drop, while PHEV sales declined 10.3%.

The only positive number in the company’s electrification Excel sheets has to do with how many EVs were sold in comparison to everything else in the portfolio. In the first three quarters of 2026, the share of EV sales within the BMW Group reached 18.4%, up from last year’s 18%.

Things should improve once the iX3 and i3 are widely available everywhere in the world, but they’re not guaranteed to be a success in the U.S., where policy whiplash has severely slowed the adoption of all-electric vehicles.

#4493. Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Has Become One of the Highest-Rated Games Ever

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

I've been waiting for another excuse to return to Hyrule, and apparently, I won't have to wait much longer! The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is getting a fresh start with its upcoming remake, and if the first reviews are anything to go by, Nintendo might have another all-time classic on its hands.

In fact, the game has already joined a pretty exclusive club of the highest-rated titles in gaming history.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (2026), a remake of the beloved Nintendo 64 adventure originally released in 1998, has made quite an impressive debut on both Metacritic and OpenCritic, two of the biggest review aggregators in the gaming industry. And considering the legacy the original has left behind, those are some pretty big shoes to fill!

Eiji Aonuma and the development team for the Ocarina of Time remake discussed how one of the original's infamous dungeons is being improved.

At the time of writing, the remake holds an impressive 96 Metascore based on 80 critic reviews on Metacritic, earning a classification of universal acclaim. That puts it among the platform's highest-rated games of all time, with only 34 titles boasting a score of 96 or higher (excluding collections, naturally).

Interestingly, the list already has some familiar faces for Zelda fans, as Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom, and The Wind Waker are all part of that exclusive group, alongside the original Ocarina of Time, which remains the only game to achieve a perfect 99 score.

And OpenCritic tells a similar story. The remake also currently holds a 96 average score, placing it fourth on the aggregator's Best Games of All Time ranking. It's currently behind only Super Mario Odyssey (97), Baldur's Gate 3 (96), and Breath of the Wild (96), which, truth be told, are masterpieces in their own right!

Google's newest easter egg allows you to revisit the past with the power of the Master Sword.

That's quite an achievement for a game revisiting an adventure that many players already consider one of the greatest ever made. It's especially fitting that the remake arrives as part of the celebrations surrounding The Legend of Zelda's 40th anniversary, giving Nintendo the perfect opportunity to bring one of its most iconic adventures to a new generation.

Of course, this isn't simply a fresh coat of paint. The remake introduces modernized graphics, a free camera system, and even a dedicated jump button, bringing several changes to how players experience Link's journey through Hyrule while preserving the adventure that made the original so memorable.

It's especially fitting that the remake arrives as part of the celebrations surrounding The Legend of Zelda's 40th anniversary, giving Nintendo the perfect opportunity to bring one of its most iconic adventures to a new generation.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launches exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5. And honestly, I don't think I'll need much convincing to revisit this particular adventure – and I have a feeling I'm not alone in that. The moment the game becomes available, I'll probably be too busy exploring Hyrule and getting lost in one of my favorite Zelda games all over again. With reviews this impressive, I have a feeling plenty of players will be doing exactly the same!

#4492. BYD’s electric hypercar hits 312 mph, first production car over 500 km/h

BYD’s Yangwang U9 Xtreme just reached 503.17 km/h (312.66 mph) on a closed highway in Abu Dhabi, making it the first production car ever to go faster than 500 km/h.

The FIA and Guinness World Records both recognized the run. It’s the all-electric hypercar’s second top-speed record in just over a year, and the one it broke was its own.

BYD announced the record on X this morning, saying the U9 Xtreme “has done the impossible” and calling it “the fastest production car on the planet.”

Abu Dhabi closed a 10 km section of the Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed International Road (E11), in the emirate’s Al Dhafra Region, for the attempt. That gave the team a 7 km straight. Marc Basseng, the German racing driver who set the car’s previous record, was behind the wheel again.

It took two days. Basseng maxed out at 490 km/h on the first day, per the FIA. After an overnight round of changes to the rear wing, damping, and tire pressures, he got to 503.17 km/h on his second attempt of November 1.

The previous mark was 496.22 km/h (308 mph), set at Germany’s ATP Papenburg proving ground in September 2025. That run had already pushed the Bugatti Chiron Super Sport 300+ and its 490.48 km/h from 2019 off the top of the list.

And it comes just days after BYD released footage of a U9 Xtreme crashing into a guardrail at about 280 mph during an earlier high-speed test. The driver walked away unharmed. BYD went right back out and hit 457.89 km/h on the next run.

The U9 Xtreme is the track-focused version of the Yangwang U9, the flagship supercar from BYD’s luxury brand. It uses four electric motors, each rated at 555 kW and spinning up to 30,000 rpm, for 2,220 kW combined. That’s over 3,000 PS, or nearly 3,000 hp.

It runs on a 1,200-volt architecture with a track-grade version of BYD’s Blade Battery. Those are LFP cells, the same chemistry BYD puts in its cheapest city cars.

For context, the Rimac Nevera R, which snagged a pile of EV world records last year, tops out at 431.45 km/h. The U9 Xtreme also holds the production EV lap record at the Nürburgring Nordschleife at 6:59.157.

Only 30 will be built, and BYD is charging around $3 million apiece. Don’t expect to see one in the US, where BYD doesn’t sell passenger cars.

The biggest one: this is a single-direction run. The two Guinness titles listed for the attempt, highest speed by a production car and by an electric production car, are both specified as “single direction.” BYD’s post claims four Guinness records, but the FIA’s announcement only lists those two for this run.

Production car top speed records have traditionally been the average of two runs in opposite directions, within an hour, to cancel out wind and road grade. That’s how Koenigsegg got its 447.19 km/h record with the Agera RS in 2017.

Bugatti took heat for exactly this in 2019, when the Chiron hit 490 km/h one way on a pre-production car. Bugatti itself said it wasn’t an official record.

The car also ran on bespoke semi-slick tires developed with Giti Tire. It’s not clear whether the 30 customer cars will get them.

A Chinese automaker best known for $10,000 city cars now builds the fastest production car in the world, and it’s electric. Not long ago, the conventional wisdom was that EVs couldn’t sustain high top speeds because the battery and motors would overheat long before the car ran out of road. BYD just ran 503 km/h on LFP cells. LFP cells!

But we’d hold BYD to the same standard we held Bugatti to. A one-way run on a highway with a 7 km straight is a great demo, not a definitive record, but impressive nonetheless.

And either way, let’s be honest: this is about marketing. Nobody is going to drive one of these 30 cars at 500 km/h. But it works. It’s a halo for Yangwang ahead of its new ultra-luxury sedan and for BYD’s push into Europe, and it makes the “Chinese cars are cheap copies” crowd look out of date.

Meanwhile, Tesla promised a Roadster that would hit over 250 mph back in 2017. Nine years later, it’s still not in production.

The real question now is whether Bugatti or Koenigsegg answers with a two-way 500 km/h run. Koenigsegg says its Jesko Absolut can theoretically do it, but it has never attempted a run. Is BYD what finally makes them try?

#4490. China’s Electric Supercar Slayer Just Did Something No Production Car Has Ever Done

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

A Chinese EV is officially the fastest production car in the world and the first production car in history to break the 500 kilometers per hour (310 miles per hour) barrier. BYD’s Yangwang U9 Xtreme, a two-door electric hypercar, reached 503.17 kph (310.7 mph) on a public road in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, on November 1.

As a reminder, the U9 Xtreme was already the world’s fastest car, after it reached 496.22 kph (308.3 mph) back in September 2025, but the Chinese automaker had already set its sights last year on breaking the 500 kph barrier—something that no other production car has ever managed.

The latest and most impressive record happened on a roughly 10-kilometer (6.2-mile) stretch of the E11 road in Abu Dhabi’s Al Dhafra Region, which was closed to public traffic. German racing driver Marc Basseng, the same driver who delivered the previous record, was behind the wheel and needed four runs over the course of two days to set the new record.

The first two runs happened on October 31, when the maximum speed was 490 kph (304.4 mph). Engineers made adjustments to the vehicle’s aerodynamics, suspension settings, and tire pressures to improve stability and performance. Then, on the last run of the second day, the Racelogic recorder made the 503.17 kph (310.7 mph) run official.

According to Guinness World Records, the Yangwang U9 Xtreme now holds the records for the highest speed achieved by a production car and an electric production car in a single-direction run. The FIA also confirmed the achievement on its website.

That last part is particularly interesting because the usual way of breaking records involves two separate runs in opposite directions to account for elevation change, wind speed, and any potential breakdown. BYD went for a single run in a single direction, which could make companies like Rimac, Bugatti, and Koenigsegg raise an eyebrow and challenge BYD’s result.

Nevertheless, going over 500 kph in a production car—albeit a limited-production model—is immensely impressive, especially considering that it’s an EV. BYD plans to make just 30 units of the U9 Xtreme, which is the most powerful and fastest version of the U9 supercar. Powered by four electric motors totaling 2,977 horsepower, the Xtreme uses a 1,200-volt lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery pack that can discharge at a 30C rate. A set of semi-slick GitiSport e-GTR2 Pro tires keeps the car on the road and provides stopping power, helped by titanium calipers and carbon-ceramic rotors.
