#4390. New Honkai Title Enters Final Closed Beta Before Launch

Michael Manning (He/Him) has been enamored with video games since he first played the Sonic Classic Collection as a child. With decades of experience in gaming and a full tour as a Gaming Journalist, Michael is ready to step up to the plate. From AAA to the smallest passion projects, his motto is that every piece of ar

While some series focus on honing in directly on a gameplay niche, others make their mark with constant reinvention, shifting and trying out whatever’s hot at the current moment. While it may not always work, with proper care, these titles can shift from trend-chasers to iterations with proper value, introducing fans, new and old, to all-new ways to play.

Wuthering Waves is one of the biggest Gachas on the planet, and they do far better than most at answering player complaints. Let's go over exactly how!

HoYoverse is one such studio, never shy about trying something new with both original titles and new entries in their larger Honkai franchise. The newest title in that franchise, Honkai: Nexus Anima, is approaching its final closed beta, implementing full playable versions of its creature acquiring, base building, and auto-battler combat, a far cry from the action RPGs and turn-based trades the franchise is now known for.

At this point it’s becoming a little difficult to define the “Honkai style” when it comes to actual gameplay, a fact HoYoverse doesn’t seem all that afraid of. While the original heavy hitter for the studio, Honkai: Third Impact, was an action RPG, the success of Honkai: Star Rail has made it clear that what fans really expect from the name Honkai is the sci-fi trappings and HoYoverse's seal of quality the studio is known for.

Continuing the trend of constant change, Honkai: Nexus Anima feels like a mix of creature catcher and auto-chess, a wild fusion of Pokémon and Teamfight Tactics that feels strangely perfect. The game’s final closed beta, which is currently open for registration and starts on November 26th, will be as close to launch-feature complete as possible, showcased in a new gameplay video that goes through all the major mechanics.

Unlike other HoYoverse titles that ask players to pull for both characters and their weapons, Nexus Anima focuses on both larger characters with unique abilities, known as Eidos, and the creatures used to make up teams, called Anima.

Obtaining an Eidos will grant an immediate copy of their matching Anima, offering a series power boost and making pulling for Eidos directly more outwardly profitable. Alongside pulling for some banner Anima, many can be found and caught directly in the wild, providing the basis for your team to be empowered by higher-tiered creatures.

Alongside the auto-battler combat, Nexus Anima puts a major focus on exploration and personal base building, allowing you to spend time with your Anima and potentially attract extra. Anima also provide a variety of exploration benefits as you catch them, serving as mounts for faster movement or mobility tools to open up otherwise inaccessible areas.

HoYoverse is seriously skilled at making beautiful, out-of-this-world settings that fuse fantasy and technology to great effect. Nexus Anima seems to be their answer to other exploration-focused titles that have released recently, with the extra spin of creature collection doing wonders to incentivize that exploration.

While it may not always work, with proper care, these titles can shift from trend-chasers to iterations with proper value, introducing fans, new and old, to all-new ways to play.

Despite how much HoYoverse has done to define the baseline of the modern Gacha space, it’s great to see them really shake things up, offering a truly different vibe than the Action RPG hybrids that dominate the space. While the rest of the genre is trying to play catch-up, HoYoverse is giving the people what they never knew they wanted.

Competing with HoYoverse polish is a struggle for their biggest competitors, and while an auto-battler may seem like a small market, the success of Teamfight Tactics across the globe makes it clear there’s a market. Nexus Anima’s cozy side offerings make it the perfect choice for the gamer who just wants something low-stress to log into after a long day, a niche that’s only grown over the years.

Arc Raiders has delivered a big new update that's very fittingly on theme, and it's not without new mechanics.

Arc Raiders is kicking off its last major event of the year. The Cold Snap update arrives moments from now, and it’s perhaps the game’s biggest since its momentous launch in late October. We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including new content - that all players have access to.

The other event is the Candleberry Banquet Project, which requires you to donate items found on the surface (including Candleberries).

While on the subject, the new update also kicks off a new Raider Deck (battle pass). Available from December 26, The Goalie Raider Deck is pretty much what you’d expect. You’ll find several pages of cosmetic and useful items. The new Deck will be available to all players for free.

#4388. Major trial challenges how doctors decide who really needs statins

A major clinical trial has raised new questions about how doctors decide who should take statins to prevent heart attacks and strokes. Researchers found that using heart scans to guide treatment decisions produced the same observed rate of major cardiovascular events as traditional risk assessments, even though the scans led to far fewer recommendations to begin taking statins.

The findings, presented during a Hot Line session at ESC Congress 2026, also revealed a striking difference in how consistently patients took their medication. Those advised to use statins based on calcium buildup in their coronary arteries were substantially more likely to follow their treatment recommendations.

Although the results suggest that heart scans could help doctors make more targeted treatment decisions, the trial did not establish that the scan approach was as effective as conventional risk assessment. Researchers say additional studies are needed to determine whether it offers a better strategy for preventing cardiovascular disease.

Why Predicting Heart Disease Risk Remains a Challenge

Cardiovascular disease remains the world's leading cause of illness and death. Much of this burden comes from atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), which develops when fatty deposits known as plaque accumulate inside arteries, restricting blood flow and increasing the risk of heart attacks and strokes. Coronary artery disease and ischemic stroke are two major forms of this condition.

Several common factors increase the likelihood of developing ASCVD, including smoking, diabetes, high blood pressure, and elevated cholesterol. Doctors use these factors to estimate a person's cardiovascular risk and determine whether preventive medications are appropriate.

Statins are among the most widely used treatments for lowering that risk. These medications reduce cholesterol levels, particularly low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, often called LDL or bad cholesterol. They also help lower the likelihood of serious cardiovascular complications.

However, identifying which patients stand to benefit from statins remains a significant challenge. Some people who eventually experience a heart attack do not appear to be at particularly high risk under conventional screening methods.

"For far too many patients, the first symptom of ASCVD is a heart attack," said Doctor Joseph B Muhlestein from the Intermountain Medical Center, Murray, USA, the Principal Investigator of the CorCal Outcomes trial. "Statins have been shown to be highly effective in the prevention of ASCVD; however, there is a major gap in risk assessment, statin initiation, and statin persistence."

According to Muhlestein, many people who suffer their first heart attack, particularly younger adults, would not previously have been classified as having enough cardiovascular risk to justify statin treatment. This limitation has prompted researchers to investigate whether directly examining the arteries might provide more useful information.

Can Heart Calcium Scans Improve Statin Decisions?

The CorCal Outcomes trial investigated two different approaches for determining which patients should be advised to begin statin therapy before experiencing a cardiovascular event.

The first relied on the pooled cohort equations (PCE), a commonly used risk assessment tool that estimates cardiovascular risk using traditional factors such as age, cholesterol levels, blood pressure, and smoking status.

The second approach measured coronary artery calcium (CAC), which provides a more direct indication of plaque buildup in the arteries supplying the heart.

This measurement uses a computed tomography (CT) scan to detect calcium deposits in the coronary arteries. Calcium can accumulate within atherosclerotic plaque, making it a useful marker of underlying coronary artery disease, even in people who have not developed symptoms.

Unlike traditional risk calculators, which estimate the likelihood of future cardiovascular problems based on personal characteristics and health measurements, calcium scans provide evidence of disease already present in the coronary arteries.

Researchers wanted to determine whether using this information to guide statin recommendations could improve cardiovascular outcomes.

Nearly 5,800 Patients Put Both Methods to the Test

The trial enrolled 5,772 patients from the Canyons and Desert regions of Intermountain Health Care in the United States. Participants had no known history of ASCVD or diabetes and had not previously received statin therapy.

Their average age was 64, and women accounted for 51% of the study population.

Eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to one of two groups. One group received statin treatment guidance based on traditional cardiovascular risk scores, while the other received recommendations based on coronary calcium scan results.

Both patients and their physicians were informed of the treatment recommendations generated by the study protocol. However, the final decision about whether to start taking statins remained with the patients and their doctors.

The researchers then tracked major cardiovascular events (MACE; all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and arterial revascularization).

This combined outcome included death from any cause, heart attacks, strokes, and procedures to restore blood flow through narrowed or blocked arteries.

Heart Scans Led to Far Fewer Statin Recommendations

After an average follow-up of 4.2 years, researchers found that major cardiovascular events occurred at exactly the same observed rate in both groups.

A total of 2.7% of patients in each group experienced one of the events included in the study's primary outcome. The estimated relative risk over time was also nearly identical (hazard ratio 0.99; 95% confidence interval 0.71 to 1.38; p=0.045 for noninferiority).

However, this similarity did not establish that the two strategies were equally effective. The study failed to meet its predetermined statistical requirement for demonstrating that the calcium scan approach was not meaningfully worse than conventional risk assessment.

A notable difference emerged in how frequently patients were advised to begin taking statins.

Participants evaluated using traditional risk scores received recommendations to start statin therapy more than three times as often as those whose decisions were guided by coronary calcium measurements.

Despite this substantial difference in treatment recommendations, both groups experienced the same observed rate of major cardiovascular events during the follow-up period.

A Surprising Difference in Statin Adherence

Perhaps the most intriguing finding involved whether patients actually followed their prescribed treatment.

Among those advised to take statins, patients whose recommendations were based on calcium scans were much more likely to adhere to their medication regimen than those assessed using traditional cardiovascular risk factors.

The difference was substantial (62% vs. 23%).

In other words, patients recommended statins based on visible evidence of calcium buildup in their arteries were approximately 2.7 times as likely to follow their medication regimen.

One possible explanation is that seeing evidence of disease in their own arteries makes patients more motivated to take preventive medication. However, the trial did not establish why adherence differed so dramatically between the groups.

The findings raise the possibility that coronary calcium scans could influence not only which patients receive statin recommendations, but also whether those patients consistently take the medications.

What the Findings Mean for Heart Disease Prevention

Despite these potentially important differences, the researchers emphasized that the study could not establish whether calcium scan-guided treatment provides cardiovascular protection comparable to traditional risk assessment.

One important limitation was that fewer participants experienced major cardiovascular events than the investigators had anticipated. With fewer events to analyze, the trial had less statistical power to determine whether a meaningful difference existed between the two approaches.

"The power of the study to detect a difference was reduced by the lower-than-expected event rates and we did not demonstrate noninferiority between the groups," said Doctor Muhlestein, who concluded: "The study did provide important hypothesis-generating insights into the efficiency of statin initiation and adherence when decisions are based on CAC scoring. Taken together, our data could be used to plan an additional well-powered randomized trial comparing CAC with current risk factor-based algorithms."

The findings may help researchers design future trials capable of determining whether coronary calcium scans can improve the efficiency of statin prescribing without compromising cardiovascular protection.

Current European recommendations already recognize a potential role for these measurements. The 2025 Focused Update of the 2019 ESC/EAS Guidelines for the management of dyslipidemias recommends considering increased coronary calcium scores, when available, as an additional factor in cardiovascular risk assessment.

This guidance applies particularly to people at moderate cardiovascular risk or those whose estimated risk falls near the threshold at which preventive medication would normally be recommended.

For these individuals, evidence of calcium buildup may help doctors make more informed decisions when the need for statin therapy is uncertain.

The CorCal Outcomes findings add to the discussion by suggesting that heart scans may also influence how faithfully patients follow treatment. Whether that advantage translates into better long-term cardiovascular outcomes remains an important question for future research.

#4387. Phantom Blade Zero Review – Wuxia Wonder Abounds

Rooted in Wuxian storytelling and scale, built on an impressively detailed combat system, and wrapped in a bloody Chinese martial underground that’s a genuine joy to play in, Phantom Blade Zero is a feat. It joins an echelon of action pedigree that includes Sekiro, Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, and just about any other action game you hold in high regard. It hails from developer S-Game, which has dabbled in mobile and smaller-scale games, and I’m shocked by what it’s pulled off with its triple-A action inauguration. But make no mistake: though Phantom Blade Zero is this team’s first crack at a game like this, it is an incredibly confident, strong debut.

Protagonist Soul is a stoic martial arts master betrayed by the Order he’s sworn his life to; he dies and returns to life with only 66 days to live. That’s enough time to settle his debts, repay his betrayers, and end a villainous conspiracy to seize full power of the Wulin realm. This narrative is Phantom Blade Zero's weakest link, but its premise adds enough mystery and tension to keep this Wuxian journey exciting through to its final, realm-shattering moments. Narrative bombshells drop not just through the game’s general fantasy-realism art direction, but also through anime scenes, opera puppet shows, animated brushstroke sequences, and more, highlighting Chinese culture and its integral place in Phantom Blade Zero.

The game features a staggering number of unique enemy types, and though the final hours get a bit repetitive, it’s admirable how long S-Game maintains such a high level of combat-oriented ecstasy. Soul’s access to weapons drives that exhilaration. Every weapon is wholly unique. Because the combat is combo-based, picking up a new weapon feels like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. Each has its own moveset and abilities, with later-game weapons featuring combo lists that look more at home in a Street Fighter menu. Add in the special, tide-turning weapons known as Phantom Edges, with limited charge-based uses, and there’s no shortage of permutations to delightfully experiment with.

Drawing on Chinese cinema, Phantom Blade Zero's setpiece bosses boast a sense of awe and scale only the genre's best typically offer. With virtually no repeat bosses, save for a few in separate trials, it’s impressive how many powerful figures I flayed, and how many delivered a unique fight. I also appreciate the checkpoints between boss phases, as they remove the frustrating repetition of replaying phase one again and again just to take another stab at the second phase I’m struggling with.

You’d be forgiven for assuming Phantom Blade Zero is a Soulslike, given its challenging bosses, interconnected world, and Phantom Bell checkpoints, this game’s equivalent of bonfires. It definitively isn’t, though. The challenge is much more surmountable; the game isn’t interested in making you die over and over, there are difficulty options, and you can equip accessories to make parries and dodges easier. World progression is materially different, too, as enemies don’t respawn after you kill them. It’s an interesting, perhaps blasphemous, choice for the genre, but it's surprisingly effective, adding a sense of worldbuilding and tangible progression I didn’t know I wanted from my action games. Soul is on a mission to remove evil, and mechanically, I’m doing just that. Enemies don’t respawn incoherently just because I heal and save.

Environmental features weave in and out of each other, and the architectural design and layout of these regions lead to many subsequent “aha” moments. S-Game infuses search-action elements into this exploration through the aforementioned Phantom Edges, some of which double as tools to unlock surprising new areas in both new and previously visited biomes. As a result, backtracking and exploration remain fresh. A lot of it is optional, as are some of Phantom Blade Zero's most rewarding elements, including its demanding “perfect” ending. Sadly, this renders other endings unsatisfying, with clear chunks intentionally missing.

Despite forays into the Uncanny Valley, Phantom Blade Zero is visually striking, and the action is brilliantly animated. It’s all set to genre-breaking music, too, with original metalcore songs, operatic choirs, 808s, and traditional Chinese instrumentation, creating a score as illustrious as the action it enhances.

Phantom Blade Zero is an astounding action achievement, almost unbelievably so for a game that is essentially a studio’s genre debut. It is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, one that recognizes the genre’s strengths and weaknesses and addresses both with fantastical Wuxian style. Though the action genre is always jam-packed with new releases, few are as special as Phantom Blade Zero.

#4386. Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

The last major Arc Raiders update of the year has arrived, bringing several big new features to the game, but not without some bad news.

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a new conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

To start with, today’s update finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer said the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock new Raider Decks immediately after release.

The good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

The Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark says this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

As for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

And, of course, it wouldn’t be a big Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

The Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.

Legend of Kingdoms is a relaxing gacha RPG that focuses on a simple formula: battle, more battle, and a little bit of gacha. I've been playing since release (as much as time allowed), and I did manage to get a few hundred summons under my belt. So, I tried out several heroes to see how well they perform. Before we dive into more details and the tier list, though, there are a couple of things we need to talk about.

Can you get the best heroes as F2P? There are plenty of IAPs here - after all, it's a gacha - but that won't keep you from getting enough heroes to make some significant upgrades and progress in the story mode. You can get a lot of Jades and Recruit Tickets (like I mentioned earlier), and those will be enough to get you clearing the early levels without much hassle.

In the late game, it will be a little tougher, but if you give it enough time and do all of your dailies (and everything else you can), you will get enough heroes - maybe even some of the best heroes in Legend of Kingdoms. Who knows?

All the heroes at the bottom of this Legend of Kingdoms tier list should only be used as fodder and nothing else. You can't really make them work into any team, and there is no point in doing that either. You can upgrade them so you can advance your main heroes, but don't bother levelling them up (even at the start).

I don't suggest you reroll in Legend of Kingdoms, since it will get you nowhere. There are a couple of good starter heroes that you already get at the beginning, plus lots of recruit tickets from the story, login, events, and codes - you name it.

You can nab a few selective summons, too, so if you didn't score some of the best-ranked heroes from the normal gacha, you can use that to get whoever you're missing. You'll need all the heroes you can get (plus dupes) to upgrade your main ones, so rerolling will put you behind. Therefore, no, you shouldn't waste time rerolling. It's pointless. If you want to do something to improve your team, redeem these Legend of Kingdoms codes as they will give you a nice starting edge.

#4383. It’s official: Battlefield 6 is 2025's best-selling game, but Black Ops 7 still managed to be November’s top-seller

2025 will be remembered for many things, but in the ultra-competitive games industry, it’s going to be thought of as the year Battlefield 6 did what many thought couldn’t happen.

Circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated. For one, November is always one of the most lucrative for the games industry, but this year in particular has seen several major hits - including new entries in two rival series.

We’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series. The decades-old fight to claim the top spot has long been won by Call of Duty, but the latest Battlefield has achieved what many thought was impossible.

Cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S. November 2025 saw spending fall by 4% compared to November 2024, bringing in a total of $5.9 billion.

Software technically saw growth during the month, but declines in hardware, and accessories were mainly responsible for the drop in overall spending. Black Ops 7 continued Call of Duty’s 18-Year Streak in topping sales in its launch month.

However, this year’s game did not also top the year-to-date charts, something the series has done consistently, and more than any other top-selling game each year - with rare exceptions. Battlefield 6 is firmly in the lead there, cementing its claim as 2025’s best-selling title. Black Ops 7, fittingly, occupies in the #7 spot there.

Separately from the best-selling game title fight, November has actually been one of the worst for the industry in terms of hardware sales. The report notes that the three major platform holders - Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all seen their hardware sales decline.

Spending on hardware during November amounted to only $695 million, a massive 27% decline compared to November 2024. According to the report, that’s the worst dollar amount total for any November since 2005, when it comes to hardware specifically. All three current-gen consoles totaled 1.6 million units sold, which Circana also notes is the lowest for any November since 1995.

This all doesn’t bode especially well for the industry. November has always been a key holiday shopping month, but it’s clear the constantly rising console prices - and already high game prices - have had a big impact.

To start with, Version 2.5 arrives on December 30, making it the game’s last major update of the year, which also means players are in for some freebies to celebrate the new year.

Narratively, this particular chapter will reveal the fate of Waifei Peninsula. The quest is gonna take the squad deeper into the Lumite Mine ruins, and the new Perception Technique is how you’ll uncover the answers hidden within.

#4380. Nintendo Indie World Showcase Recap: Everything We Saw

The year is nearing its conclusion, and the last big AAA titles are rolling out one-by-one. But today, it was all about the independent titles on Nintendo's latest Indie World Showcase, highlighting new games from smaller indie teams coming to the Switch and Switch 2.

Here's everything we saw at the October 2026 Nintendo Indie World Showcase.

Today's Indie World Showcase started with a big headliner, as the long-awaited witch-life simulator Witchbrook got a release date. Chucklefish and Robtality's cozy magical world goes live on January 28, 2027.

Fans of 3D platformers should probably keep an eye on Winds of Viridia, which looks like a colorful game with a lot of interesting movement and exploration. Shark Jump's fantastical platformer is arriving next year, but if the wait's too long, a free demo is coming today on the eShop.

From one of the co-creators of Celeste, City of None has a gorgeous pixelated art style and colors that immediately remind me of Game Boy Color classics. It's a 2D platformer where you leap around, fight enemies, and explore the strange city around you. The jumping and fighting look solid, and I really like the mysterious atmosphere and art direction. City of None's set for sometime in 2027.

The sword-surfing adventure from the makers of Abzu and Journey is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 on October 29, 2026 - tomorrow! It's a gorgeous adventure that earned a Must-Play badge from us, so it's worth your time if you like the kinds of gorgeous, beautiful adventures Giant Squid (developer of Abzu) is known for.

Take an overhead camera angle, brawler gameplay, and some John Wick sensibilities, and you've got Tenjutsu, a stylish roguelike where you use your martial arts prowess to tear apart crime syndicates. I really enjoy the look and vibe of this one, and it's from one of the designers of Dead Cells, too. Tenjutsu might be one to keep an eye on when it arrives on Switch 2 in 2027.

RPG fans have been eating well, and it looks like the feast could continue next year with Threads of Time. The time-traveling RPG is coming to both Switch and Switch 2 next summer, and it's looking absolutely gorgeous.

Ah, raccoons. Nature's most adorable little scamps. If you and your friends have ever wanted to live out the dream of being a rambunctious band of raccoons wreaking havoc on the town, Dumpster Gang sets out to give you just that fantasy in March 2027.

I've already enjoyed quite a bit of Super Battle Golf on PC, so I'll tell you now: if you enjoy golf games and want some Mario Party annoy-your-friends antics wound around them, Super Battle Golf should be on your radar for its March 25, 2027 launch on Switch 2.

Another port of a PC multiplayer mainstay, the co-op physics-driven horror-looter R.E.P.O. is coming to Switch 2 in 2027. This is one for the crowd that likes to be scared one moment and laughing hysterically the next.

Rounding out the co-op section, Haunted Paws has you and a pal playing as a pair of pups searching for their person in a haunted mansion. The side-scrolling 3D look makes it seem like a less-scary Little Nightmares, and the concept is pretty fun. Look for this one on Switch and Switch 2 in May 2027, or try out the free demo later today.

Enjoy shrines, towns, and strange night-time journeys into the unknown? Follow a fox girl and her frog friend on an adventure through a strange island in Kitsune: The Journey of Adashino on Switch 2 and Switch in spring 2027. I've said it a few times in this recap, but wow, the art here is great.

The second entry in the slime-collecting, home-building sim adventure is coming to Switch 2. Pick up adorable slimes with your vacuum, build a home for them, and explore the Rainbow Island around you in January 2027. Plus, there's an exclusive in-game item for the Switch 2 version.

From the makers of Cozy Grove, this multiplayer game encourages players to build a home above the clouds with friends and explore the world around them. Spirit Crossing looks like a big world to make your own alongside your pals, starting November 16, 2026 on both Switch and Switch 2.

Want something a little sillier? My Arms Are Longer Now is a game about, well, really long arms. With numerous Australian comedians lending their vocal talents to the project, this seems like it could be a quirky, charming, and delightfully funny experience when it arrives on both Switch and Switch 2 on March 11, 2027.

The delightfully Game Boy-styled critter delivery game Petal Runner is aiming for a full launch. I've played a bit of this one at events over the years, and it's charmed me every time. If you like nostalgic adventures with a surprisingly heartfelt core, you should mark down the March 8, 2027 launch, or check out the free demo arriving later today.

The chaotic coin-pushing game Raccoin is coming to Nintendo Switch 2. It's just like those token-shoving games you remember from arcades but with a number of wild and wacky means of pushing even more coins over the edge run-over-run. Raccoin: Chaos Max Edition hits Switch 2 on November 10, 2026, and a free demo is out later today.

Lagertha is a Champion and Infantry hero. She has an incredibly good skill, Thunderstrike, which gives her a massive buff while also allowing her to deal insane damage. With this ability, Lagertha will attack the strongest enemy while also buffing her own attack speed.

Personally, Lagertha is one of my favourite heroes in Heroes of History since her kit allows her to be pretty tanky while excelling in the damage department at the same time. At Awaken V, she will become unstoppable, having received additional ATK% at Awaken I and III, for a total of 47.5% increased ATK and a whopping 130% Crit DMG. Robin Hood is a Champion and Ranged hero. His ability primarily targets the furthest enemy, dealing a truckload of damage. He is a single-target character, but his ability can obliterate the unfortunate target he focuses on. He works exceptionally well against bosses.

With Robin Hood, you might want some additional support that reduces the enemy DEF, since Robin Hood's Sherwood's Vengeance ability will also inflict a burn, dealing additional damage over time. I'd recommend having a good tank to hold the front line until his burn takes effect..

Albert Einstein is a Genius and Siege hero. With his Everything is Relative ability, he can summon a black hole that moves around the battlefield, continuously dealing damage to enemies. He is one of the best Siege heroes you could possibly summon, and that's how he's earned a spot at the top of this Heroes of History tier list.

While your enemies are under attack by the black hole, their attack speed is also severely depleted, making them almost unable to cast their normal attacks. He is an absolute beast in terms of heroes, and once you get him to Awaken IV, his ATK will greatly increase. At Awaken V, he will cast the ability much more often, but that is not easy to achieve.

#4371. Legendary game creator Vince Zampella has passed away

Vince Zampella, co-creator of Call of Duty, and a veteran studio head responsible for some of the biggest franchises in the world, is gone.

Vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

Zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

Respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA said in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he showed up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”

#4370. RAID: Shadow Legends best champions sorted by rarity

Updated on November 5th, 2026 -  Version: 11.85.5

Having some of the best champions on your team can make a huge difference when challenging bosses and other monsters. This RAID: Shadow Legends tier list covers all of them, and it will help you pick the best in terms of usability and rarity.

Of course, as you might already know, there are quite a lot of champions. They are divided by rarity, role, affinity and faction, but don't let that discourage you - choosing the best of the best is quite simple.

First, you should learn some of the basics from our guide. Then, you should focus on just a few characters - it really doesn't matter which rarity (as long as it's not Common or Uncommon, of course), so long as they are considered S-tier. Finally, if you want to quickly upgrade them all, you should stay active. By logging in daily and doing all your quests, you'll end up levelling up and upgrading most of the champions to max rank sooner or later!

Ultimate RAID: Shadow Legends tier list Since many of these champions have multiple uses, this tier list will reflect their overall rating. I am well aware that some of the champions might do better than others in Clan Boss, for example, while others will be completely terrible for Clan Boss but S-tier for PvP Arena.

Below are all the characters released in the latest version, but their ranking is still relatively temporary - we need to test them out a little bit more! So, if you feel like some of the tiers need to be adjusted, let us know why!

The Mythical champions are the latest addition, and they are fairly similar to Legendary, except a lot stronger. If you are lucky and get a few of these, your team is set. If possible, try to aim for the S-tier ones, because they'll make a great addition to ANY team. Every Mythical champion can switch between two forms, Base and Alternate

They can also change their usability, turning from Attack to Support, Support to HP, or anything else you might imagine, depending on the champion. Just make sure to equip the right gear for the type of champion, because Mythics will need alternative sets.

Siegfrung the Nephilim is one of the first Mythical champions released, and he can switch between Support and Attack, allowing for a highly versatile playstyle. He is able to deal great damage or heal the entire team, depending on which form you choose.

Gharol the Bloodmaul is an Attack or HP champion. When in HP form, he can provide great support by removing shields from enemies and taunting them, while making himself invincible. While in Attack form, he ignores part of the target's DEF and attacks multiple times.

These are the champions you want on your team. If you manage to get a few of these, then you're probably set. Make sure that you stick to the S-tier or A-tier Legendary champions because these will greatly outshine every other character in the game.

Chaagur can inflict Sleep upon the enemy and has AoE attacks in his kit that can also inflict a Poison effect. He's an overall decent unit that also benefits from some self-sustain from the passive skill.

Lyssandra is a great character who will transfer all of her debuffs upon the target and fully drain their turn meter. She will also buff allies' SPD, allowing them to attack more often by filling up their turn meter

The Epic champions can be upgraded a lot faster than the Legendary, so you will probably end up maxing out some of these first. Try to stick to the S-tier and A-tier Epic champions if possible - in certain situations, they could even be better than the Legendarys.

Archmage Hellmut is a unit obtainable from the Doom Tower, and he's one of the best Epic characters in Raid: Shadow Legends you can get your hands on. His attacks fill up his turn meter by a lot more than they usually do for most of the other units, and his normal attacks can inflict Stun upon enemies.

Ursala the Mourner is a decent support that can reduce the enemy's DMG dealt and can also revive allies - it's super handy if you need a support unit with various debuffs in their kit

Rare champions can be okay if you don't have anything better. You can upgrade some Rare RAID champions until you get Epic or Legendary ones.

#4369. Ocarina of Time Remake Director and Producer Credit Younger Developers for Vital Modern Perspective

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

The full remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has launched for the Nintendo Switch 2 today, and perhaps unsurprisingly, the response is quite positive. It’s still an excellent game after all these years, and the modern changes, both in its presentation and gameplay tweaks, improve the overall experience without detracting from the original’s timeless charm.

Hyrule has never looked better as they look in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, and critics seem to agree!

It still feels like just yesterday when the original game launched for the Nintendo 64 in 1998, and a lot has changed in the industry since then. Heck, people who weren’t even born yet when that game came out are now working in game development, and apparently, some of those people also worked on the Ocarina of Time remake.

In an interview with The Verge, the remake’s director Hidemaro Fujibayashi and producer Eiji Aonuma, who was also the director on the original game, spoke about the vital perspectives that the team’s younger developers brought to the table in bringing the remake to life, including a few that have never even played the original. It was thanks in part to this next generation of devs that this fantastic meeting of gameplay history was able to take shape.

To paraphrase a bit of wisdom from a better writer than myself, the norms of the gaming industry are kind of like rings on a tree stump. Through various indicators in design, you can trace back the norms and common sense of game development through the ages.

The norms of the gaming industry are kind of like rings on a tree stump.

The original Ocarina of Time, while a fantastic game, is a lot different from today’s norms in its visual and mechanical approaches, and needs to be recognized as such to create a proper modern remake. If the only people working on the remake were those who worked on and/or played the original, they would’ve just made the original again. This, as Fujibayashi and Aonuma explain, is why having younger developers on the team was so important.

Eiji Aonuma and the development team for the Ocarina of Time remake discussed how one of the original's infamous dungeons is being improved.

Despite some of them not having played the original, the younger developers on the team understood in the broad sense what made its formula work, and so strove for simple, careful additions and subtractions to bring it a little more in line with modern sensibilities.

“I feel confident that they weren’t necessarily pursuing something new for the sake of novelty when it might be unneeded and clutter the experience,” Fujibayashi said. “They’re looking for elegance. Only what is needed, only what was important in the original, and how to carry that forward as their focus.”

Aonuma and Fujibayashi’s work on the remake alongside the rest of their development team really helped to illustrate to them how much has changed in the game development pipeline since Aonuma’s heyday on the original Ocarina of Time nearly 30 years ago.

“We used to have maybe just one person designing the backgrounds, and that’s something that you couldn’t do nowadays,” Aonuma said. “A lot of the process is not so different compared to the N64 days, but the scale [is different]: There’s a lot more time involved, a lot more people involved, and because of that it can be harder to manage these teams.”

Fujibayashi also worked as the director for the modern, wide-open Zelda games like Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, which are much different beasts compared to more streamlined, linear approach of Ocarina of Time. Fujibayashi recalls being fascinated with Nintendo’s early approaches to the new conundrums of 3D back in the day, particularly with the advent of the Z-targeting system. “The solutions are something that still stick with me as a foundation for when I create 3D games,” he said.

At the end of the interview, Aonuma reflected on how diversity in game design is what gives the Zelda franchise its staying power, and how this modern take on Ocarina of Time is a good example of its ability to mix things up as much (or as little) as necessary.

“We’ve had opportunities to add to the playbook of Zelda, if you will, and the language of development,” he said. “You get to see the progression of these ideas across the franchise. And now, working with younger staff on this remake, we’re having the opportunity to bring in additional new ideas. I really look forward to the future and what’s possible coming from the new staff.”

#4365. Genshin Impact Version Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, including the long-awaited Moon Maiden Columbina

The first major Genshin Impact update in 2026 is almost here, bringing characters we've been waiting a while to play, and more besides.

Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of new content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

All players will receive 1,600 Primogems through the in-game mail. If you log in regularly, you can earn up to ten Intertwined Fates. Lantern Rite has a new outfit for Yaoyao, which is also where you have a chance to earn one 4-Star Liyue character for free.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

#4364. 5 new mobile games to try this week - November 5th, 2026

Fresh mobile picks you should give a go this week

Who doesn't love new games? We certainly do - there's just something about the exhilaration of a new title you can't wait to dive into, as the loading screen pops up and you enter a brave new world.

Of course, new mobile games are a dime a dozen these days, and who has the time to scour the iPhone, iPad and/or Android stores to catch the latest title that drops? Fret not - we've gathered a quick list of 5 new mobile games you should try this week, whether that's an undiscovered indie gem or a high-profile AAA masterpiece.

That said, you can head on over to our NEW WEEKLY MOBILE GAMES hub if you're on the hunt for more curated adventures to obsess over!

I suppose there's nothing quite like the end of the month than being reminded of your adulting responsibilities, which is probably why Bills Must Be Paid picked November 1st for an official launch. As you might expect from the title, this incremental clicker will have you struggling to, well, pay the bills - but the cathartic thing about it is that you'll at least get the satisfaction of smashing piggy banks out of it.

You'll have all kinds of hammers at your disposal for said piggy bank smashing, which, of course, costs stamina. You can't let exhaustion get the better of you, though, because, as you well know, bills must be paid - and bankruptcy quite literally means game over.

Absolum's art style was what initially caught my eye here, but honestly, the fact that it's a roguelite beat 'em up is already more than enough to pique my interest. This time around, the action-packed side-scroller is bringing mobile-optimised controls to the fray, with customisable buttons you can tinker around with to keep the four varied heroes you can choose from in tip-top shape.

And with full controller support, co-op gameplay, and cross-progression on mobile and PC, I'd say Talamh's in good hands!

I've been seeing this backpack management trend a lot lately, and given I've played my fair share of them recently, I'm not at all complaining! This time, SuperPlanet's putting the world of Stonia on offer, and despite the seemingly cutesy title (and art style), it's actually a much grimmer setting than you might expect.

The continent is apparently turning into dungeons, and it's up to Dungeon Supporter Mika to save the world. You'll step into each tile not knowing what it holds, but whether it's a fatal trap you're falling into or a bloodthirsty Mimic waiting for the right moment, you'll need to use your powers of backpack organisation to survive every run. It's the backpack handler's job to give those ungrateful heroes their supplies, after all, so you're pretty much the true hero here.

If you've still got a Halloween hangover, perhaps a little bit of Jekyll and Hyde might suffice? Heir of the Dog takes the classic tale and adds a humorous twist to it, and with charming pixel art to boot! The point-and-click mystery will have you searching high and low across Victorian London for clues on a missing dog, with plenty of hilarious hijinks in between.

The main protagonist is named Cummerbund Bandersnatch, for one thing. For another, it takes inspiration from Monty Python, so you know you're in for a treat - if you're up for shelling out $14.99 a pop!

Cute cats in a mobile game is a plus as it is in my book - even more so when there's multiple copies of them! This aptly titled platformer tasks you with creating copies of yourself to solve tricky puzzles across a strange lab, where you can use your titular Copy Cats to stack up high and reach unreachable places.

You might even need to manipulate your clones just to get your main cat to the exit, because when there's a missing cat involved, you need to do everything in your power to help it find its way back home.

#4362. Here's The Best Graphics And Performance Mode For Phantom Blade Zero On PlayStation 5

Phantom Blade Zero is out now for everyone as a console exclusive on PlayStation 5 and on PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store as well. If you missed it, it's my favorite action game of the year so far, and you can read why in Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review. That explains why I think you should check the game out; Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks will get you some key information I wish I had when I started the game; and this guide I wrote up about the requirements you need to get the best ending in Phantom Blade Zero will help you find all story-critical content in the game.

However, you're looking for advice on which of the three visual modes Phantom Blade Zero offers you should use on your PS5. This here piece is for you.

Phantom Blade Zero has three visual modes on PS5 Pro: Quality, Balanced, and Performance. I tested all three. My personal favorite was Balanced, which gives you an upscaled (checkerboarded) 4K resolution at 40 FPS, as long as you have a 120Hz TV with VRR. If you have a 120Hz TV, it likely has VRR because most major manufacturers include it with 120Hz. I like this mode because the upscaled 4K looks beautiful, just a hair less than native 4K, and if you aren't someone super trained on those details, I'd wager you won't notice the difference. The best part is that this mode offers 40 FPS gameplay, which, contrary to how math works, is halfway between 30 FPS and 60 FPS; I'm not kidding, look it up. As such, 40 FPS feels much smoother than 30 FPS, and you're still getting crisp 4K resolution. It's a win-win for me and my go-to mode when a game offers it. That said, if you don’t have a PS5 Pro, you won’t see this Balanced mode.

The Performance mode offers an upscaled 2K resolution with a pretty locked 60 FPS. Phantom Blade Zero is an extremely fast, fluid action game, so I think many people will want the buttery smoothness of 60 FPS gameplay. If that's you, pick the Performance mode. Sure, its resolution is lower, and it will look blurrier and less crisp than the other two modes, but if you aren't switching back and forth often or looking at side-by-side images, you likely won't notice.

Quality mode is native 4K resolution (absolutely beautiful, the best visual image you can get playing Phantom Blade Zero), but at 30 FPS... and for a game like this, I don't think 30 FPS does it justice. I don't really recommend this mode for combat, but if you're just waltzing around Wulin, grabbing screenshots and such, turn it on and bask in the wonders of developer S-Game's art team. Note: There is an option for ray tracing on PS5 Pro. I tested all three graphics modes with it on and off and noticed zero performance changes or issues. So, use ray tracing – it’s nice!

And, in case you missed it, below is an image of the PC system requirements and specs needed to play Phantom Blade Zero on Steam and the Epic Games Store:

#4359. d4v41 and Jinggg leave Paper Rex after 7th–8th Champions finish, Pacific place secure

Paper Rex has parted with captain d4v41 and Jinggg, two Masters Toronto winners, after an early exit at Champions 2026. With its VCT Pacific partner place secure, the Singapore organisation is rebuilding by choice as free agency opens to every region.

Paper Rex has broken up the core of its VALORANT roster. The Singapore organisation is parting with its captain and one of its best-known players as the 2027 season approaches. d4v41 had been with Paper Rex since its founding in 2020. He played first on its CS:GO roster, then moved with the team to VALORANT. Jinggg joined on 28 September 2021.

Neither player has named a destination. In the farewell video Paper Rex released, d4v41 said he was moving to a new team. Jinggg wrote on X that he was excited about what comes next. d4v41 also asked fans to keep supporting the organisation after both have gone.

The split follows a season that faded at the end. Paper Rex were runners-up at both Masters Santiago and Masters London earlier in 2026. At Champions in Shanghai, they lost 2-0 to LOUD in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 7 October. A 2-1 defeat to T1 in lower-bracket round one ended their run on 9 October. The event carried a $2,250,000 prize pool. LOUD went on to beat Team Vitality in the final.

The pair leave with a long record together. Jinggg helped Paper Rex to second place at Masters Copenhagen 2022. He was also part of the run to the Champions 2023 final, where the team were runners-up. Liquipedia lists both players in the line-up that won VCT 2025 Masters Toronto.

The changes are not forced by the league. The organisation is owned by IMPLS Entertainment Pte Ltd. Riot has cut the number of partner teams in each region from ten to eight for 2027–28. That leaves 32 across the four regions.

The Pacific format rewards that security. The eight partners receive seeded places at Kickoff in January 2027. Four further places go to teams that come through open qualifiers. Paper Rex can therefore reshape its roster without needing to qualify.

Two Masters winners on the open market could matter well beyond the Pacific. EMEA’s eight partners for 2027 are Fnatic, BBL Esports, FUT Esports, Team Heretics, Team Liquid, Gentle Mates, Karmine Corp and Team Vitality. Under Riot’s open qualifier rules, most regions require three of a team’s five players to come from that region. Teams must also keep three of five players between events to carry their progress forward. Those limits will frame how far any club can rebuild around new signings.

Khalish has been part of Paper Rex since our founding in 2020, starting first on our CS:GO Roster and transitioning with the team to VALORANT. We'll always remember the laughs, the op shots, and every achievement through the years.

From everyone at Paper Rex, we wish @d4v41vlr… pic.twitter.com/UgWKD4QfOj

Later in November, open qualifiers get under way. The season’s first Masters event follows in February 2027.

#4357. Diablo 4's long-awaited Tower and its Leaderboards enter beta today, and there's no PTR funny business this time

Diablo 4's first big moment of 2026 is nearly upon us, and it's one feature many have been looking forward to for actual years.

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as quickly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

The Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two new additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

TYLOO's withdrawal from a HyperX Retake Season 13 quarter-final in Lisbon has left their PGL Major Singapore invite in doubt on cutoff day. In Europe, fnatic are shut out of the last CS2 Major of 2026 after the final weekend's results went against them.

One walkover in Lisbon looks set to decide Asia’s line-up for the PGL Major Singapore.

Neither TYLOO nor Lynn Vision is expected to play again before the cutoff. That leaves the Asian race effectively over.

The Lisbon event was a Valve Tier 2 tournament run by Hyped and PEW PEW. It ran from 29 October to 1 November with 13 teams and a prize pool of €12,187.50. Groups were GSL-format best-of-threes, followed by single-elimination best-of-three playoffs. TYLOO are listed in joint fifth to eighth place.

IEM Beijing is a far bigger draw on paper. ESL is staging it from 2 to 8 November at the Bloomage Biotech Biohyalux ECM Arena. It is S-Tier and Valve Tier 1, with 16 teams playing for $1,250,000.

TYLOO were not alone in stepping away from Lisbon. Natus Vincere also withdrew, and the organisers cited the same Beijing commitment for both teams. For NAVI, the withdrawal leaves their Major chances unchanged. They had until 19 October to pull out, but were still registered after that deadline. The Lisbon event overlapped with PGL Masters Bucharest and finished less than a day before IEM Beijing began.

After the win over 9z, the team’s points already looked sufficient, according to TYLOO coach WeiJie ‘zhokiNg’ Zhong. By that stage, they had no choice but to play the Retake event. Before IEM Beijing, he also spoke about Dongkai ‘Jee’ Ji’s recovery and the problems the team has faced this season.

Europe holds 18 of the 32 Singapore invitations, one more than it had at Cologne. The six highest-ranked eligible European teams in the 2 November standings go straight into Stage 3.

The fight for the final European spot went to the last weekend. 100 Thieves beat Wildcard 2-0 in Sunday’s FiRe Last Chance final, and the European VRS now places them 18th. Elsewhere, HOTU finished second at GLuck Moscow Cyber Games.

That was bad news for fnatic. Before the final, they sat 18th in Europe with no matches left. Their only route in was a 100 Thieves defeat and recalculated standings falling their way. Neither happened.

Moscow Cyber Games still produced a Major qualifier. Winners 1win earned a Stage 2 invitation to Singapore.

PGL set 2 November as the cutoff so the most recent results would shape the field. The weekend’s results did exactly that. The Singapore Major runs from 24 November to 13 December, with 32 teams and $1,250,000 in prize money.

#4354. Fans Are Freaking Out Over How Good The Resident Evil Movie Demake Is, And You Can Play It For Free

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

Remember when survival horror games were all about fixed camera angles, chunky polygonal characters, limited ammunition, and doors that took an unnecessarily long time to open?

Well, someone decided to bring all of that back with an unexpected project inspired by Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie – and fans (including myself) are absolutely loving it!

Called Zach Cregger's RESIDENT EVIL: The Video Game, this unofficial fan project was created by the developer and game producer Stefano Cagnani, who already created similar projects in the past for classic films such as Alien, Dawn of the Dead, The Crow, and more. And you can play it for free on itch.io right now by checking out the project on this page!

It is currently available for PC and reimagines the director's movie as a classic PlayStation 1 survival horror experience. And honestly, if you're anything like me and have a soft spot for the franchise's early days, this might be right up your alley.

There are several Resident Evil titles that deserve to be remade after Resident Evil Veronica.

As its name suggests, the project takes the movie's premise and gives it a nostalgic makeover, complete with everything you'd expect from a late-'90s Resident Evil game. So yes, we are talking fixed camera angles, tank controls, low-poly graphics, dark environments, scarce ammunition, and even those iconic close-ups of doors opening as you move between areas.

However, don't expect to experience the entire movie just yet. The current version only covers its opening sequence, following the snowy road until the protagonist reaches the farm – but it already features the appearance of one of the movie's most terrifying creatures.

Called Zach Cregger's RESIDENT EVIL: The Video Game, this unofficial fan project was created by the developer and game producer Stefano Cagnani, who already created similar projects in the past for classic films such as Alien, Dawn of the Dead, The Crow, and more.

What makes this project so interesting is how lovingly it recreates the atmosphere of classic survival horror. It's a wonderful love letter not only to Cregger's movie (which finally broke the franchise's curse of not having a genuinely good live-action film – sorry, Milla Jovovich!), but also to the early Resident Evil games that made so many of us fall in love with the series.

If you are a fan of horror titles, there are plenty of old games that should be brought back, as they were something great.

Although the project was released a few days ago, it's only now starting to gain more attention, with fans sharing gameplay footage and streaming their experiences online. And judging by the reactions, Stefano might have something pretty special on his hands.

One player was already asking for more, commenting, "Full game needs to be released as soon as possible." Another praised its nostalgic atmosphere, saying, "This looks actually pretty sick. [It] takes me back to the 90s style of Resident Evil." Not everyone was simply celebrating the throwback, though. One particularly amusing comment praised the project while taking a little jab at the movie's humor: "did they remove the constant jokes and constant humor? If so, I'm sold!"

Well, I guess you can't please everyone! Regardless, it's lovely to see a fan project capturing the attention of Resident Evil fans, especially one that understands just how much atmosphere and a few well-placed camera angles can do for a survival horror experience. So, if you've been missing the days of wandering through dark corridors with barely enough ammunition to defend yourself, this free little project might be exactly what you need.

#4353. The Sims developer vows "our values are unchanged," as it teases multiple projects from post-Saudi-owned EA

The team behind one of EA's most diverse franchises has issued a statement about its future under the soon-to-be Saudi-owned publisher.

In their (slightly belated) new years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are currently working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

This, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

Understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s new ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we plan for today, tomorrow, and the future.”

As for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of new Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Future releases, of course, include new The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.)

Some of these projects will see more playtesting throughout 2026, so you should probably sign up for The Sims Labs if you want to hear about when/how you can get involved.

#4349. Jordan Esports Federation signs MoU with King Hussein Business Park to host more events

Priya Venkatesh has been following the money in esports since before brand deals were considered legitimate marketing. She got pulled into the scene through competitive fighting games and eventually found herself more interested in the contracts and partnerships behind the tournaments than the matches themselves. These days she focuses on how brands navigate esports sponsorships, where the smart money is going, and which deals are actually built to last versus the ones that look good in a press release.

The Jordan Esports Federation (JEF) has signed a memorandum of understanding with King Hussein Business Park (KHBP) in Amman, giving the national body a formal framework to stage more tournaments and events at the site it already calls home.

KHBP announced the deal on Sunday in a statement published on its website. Prince Omar bin Faisal, who is President of the JEF, attended the signing.

Under the MoU, the federation and the business park will jointly host and organise specialised competitions on the KHBP campus. They will also receive the international delegations and official guests that travel to those events. Beyond the competitive side, the two organisations plan to cooperate on media and marketing, look at shared education, training and community projects, and swap knowledge and expertise.

Neither party has disclosed financial terms or the length of the agreement.

KHBP CEO Eng. Ammar Ezzeddin presented the MoU as part of the park’s wider ambitions. “This partnership builds on our ongoing efforts to create an enabling environment for institutions, initiatives and high-potential sectors, and to establish KHBP as a hub for innovation and technology,” he said.

He added: “We look forward to helping the sector thrive and to hosting more tournaments and events that put Jordanian talent in the spotlight and raise the Kingdom’s profile in this field.”

JEF Vice President Hazem Bawab focused on the competitive and grassroots goals. “This partnership is a significant step in our drive to develop the esports industry in Jordan and elevate the standard of local, regional and international competitions and activities,” he said.

Bawab continued: “We look forward to drawing on the setup and capabilities that KHBP offers to scale our work, nurture young talent and launch joint programmes that help the industry grow and encourage greater participation.”

The deal formalises a relationship that already exists on the ground. According to The Esports Radar, the JEF, which is the government recognised regulator for esports in the country, is based at the park in West Amman.

A lot of that work happens at THE ARC, the arena and gaming dome inside the park. The same report lists past events there including the fourth Arab Esports League, a Women’s Esports Championship and Red Bull Login, which doubled as Jordan’s national final stage in Dota 2 and Counter-Strike 2. The venue is also an incubation centre supported by the federation and the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship, and runs training camps for players hoping to turn professional.

KHBP has been a destination for esports investment for some time. In 2024, lounge operator True Gamers announced plans for an esports venue in Jordan at the business park, a project in which its CPO publicly thanked the JEF and Prince Omar.

The timing also puts Amman in the industry spotlight. PocketGamer.biz points out that Pocket Gamer Connects Jordan takes place on 7 and 8 November, bringing many of the region’s games industry stakeholders to the city later this week.

Battlefield Studios has released its first official communication in 2026. Rather than unveil the second season of Battlefield 6, however, the developer instead announced a delay. The currently ongoing Season 1 was initially meant to end on Tuesday, January 20, hence why the developer had to communicate something this week.

Season 1 will now end on Tuesday, February 17, which is also when Season 2 will kick off. Given the current sentiment around the game, this news isn’t surprising in the least.

Escalating the fight with new threats on the battlefield.Season 2 begins February 17. pic.twitter.com/fGMegJJuTj

What we are getting news of today, however, is the game’s next patch. This extension update is going to arrive next week, on January 20, when Season 1 was supposed to end. It’s bringing new weekly challenges to the game, but its biggest addition is yet another Bonus Path to the battle pass. You can also expect the free daily login rewards to continue, alongside other periods of double XP.

Though the latest blog post may be devoid of any real details on Season 2, BF Studios confirmed that Battlefield Labs will play a larger role in offering a preview of what’s to come, so it’s entirely possible that the testing initiative will soon open its doors to players with an early look at some of the maps and other content planned for Season 2.
